"We can take the heat!" Are you sure about that?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Dead by Daylight's devs have found themselves in hot water and in the middle of quite a mess. In short, over the Halloween weekend a team member saw TheBurntPeanut playing Dead by Daylight, not in a sponsored stream I may add, and gifted him free DLC, items, and currency.

All the Dead by Daylight DLCs combined come to $335/£301: a substantial sum to just give away to a streamer who makes more money than most of us will see in a lifetime. TheBurntPeanut did then offer to give back all the content and said that he was willing to pay for it, but the official response from an official Dead by Daylight account on his stream was, "We can take the heat. They are yours to keep."

This turned out to be untrue, as shortly after the stream Dead by Daylight rescinded this offer. In an official social media post the devs explained: "we have already removed the content that was granted to the creator".

So what went wrong? Well, gifting hundreds of dollars worth of free stuff to a wealthy content creator who isn't undertaking a sponsored stream isn't a fantastic look. But the DBD community were more annoyed about the conflict in values. Something that the Dead by Daylight creator has now acknowledged:

"When collaborating with a new creator, we normally look thoroughly at their past content to determine whether they are representing the values of inclusion our community expects from us. In this case, this was not taken into proper consideration or discussed as a group.

"When we talk about our values in relation to our community, we mean respect, transparency, diversity, and creating a space where people from different backgrounds and experiences feel welcome. Diversity is one of DBD's core principles and everyone is welcome to play it. But when we choose to work with a creator, we're putting our name next to theirs, and we want to partner with creators whose words and actions share and support that principle."

They have also confirmed that there will be updated request and approval methods for this kind of thing going forward to ensure "any Dead by Daylight spokesperson is properly representing our team and our values."

#3888. COD Modern Warfare 4 has seemingly answered DMZ players' PvE calls with new Story Mission changes - but there are major caveats

For as long as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ extraction mode has been available, there've been calls for PvE-only servers. Developer Infinity Ward, for its part, has maintained the mode is designed as a PvPvE experience, but it's now seemingly made a change offering solo players something of a compromise, albeit with caveats.

In DMZ, your choice of deployment type dictates the matchmaking pool you're put into. You can choose to freely roam the map, picking up tasks as you go, or participate in slightly more structured Dynamic Ops which constantly generate tasks for you to do. But DMZ also has Story Missions, a title that suggests they're private instances. But that wasn't the case at launch. Although the number of players allowed into Story Mission instances appeared to be smaller than in other modes, it was still possible to run into other players, which meant potentially unwanted PvP encounters.

Now, however, Infinity Ward appears to have made Story Missions private, but only for solo players, and only when playing a Story Mission for the first time - after which, repeated attempts will be much less forgiving.

Infinity Ward has not officially announced a change, but players began noticing it on Reddit and elsewhere, and I wanted to investigate for myself: I just finished a Story Mission - a first attempt - and despite making as much noise as possible, I ran into no other players. The Recent Players list in the social tab, which displays the names of players you've recently crossed paths with, was likewise empty for me. I also noticed zero activated UAV Towers and SAM Sites - a rare sight in PvPvE matches where players always run to the former to reveal enemies around them. There's some suggestion you may still run into others in a Story Mission, however, so best not lower your guard. As welcome as the change is, it highlights the split in DMZ's community. Many would rather not cross paths with other players, and it's especially frustrating for those expecting a purely PvE mode in this year's Call of Duty.

#3887. Square Enix will ‘most likely’ focus on new games after Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, producer says

What's next? Will the fantasy finally be final?

Mainline Final Fantasy entries have taken a bit of a backseat in lieu of the FF7 remake trilogy, but that should be changing soon.

The trilogy’s producer Yoshinori Kitase teased the franchise’s future in a new interview, but I also wouldn’t hold my breath for Final Fantasy 17 launching any time soon after FF7 Revelation drops this April.

“I think that mainly we are more likely to invest in new titles and new games, but at the same time, for example, this time with the [FF7] remake, there was me and other creators who worked on the original game, which we had really strong feelings towards,” Kitase said when asked about new IP and remakes in the interview with IGN. “And we really wanted to create something new related to the old game to allow new users to play and to know the appeal of this game as much as the old users who play the old game. So there might be different cases like this one where the company is willing to invest in remaking old projects and other kinds of games like it happened this time.”

That’s…not really a definitive answer either way regarding remakes vs. new entries vs. new IP at Square, which is notoriously busy with multiple RPG releases year in and out across its numerous dev teams. For example, this year alone, the company has released Final Fantasy Resonance, The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales, Bravely Default Flying Fairy HD Remaster, and a few others.

Kitase’s words are iffy no matter how you look at it, but mainline FF entries have generally slowed down quite a bit. FF16 launched in 2023, but FF15 released way back in 2016. Meanwhile, FF7 trilogy games have come out in 2020, 2024, and next year again in 2027.

I’m generally a very big fan of the remake trilogy, and FF7 Revelation is one of my most anticipated titles of 2027, but I have a hard time imagining the company going on to remake another game… although I would not be against it, for several classic titles (6, 8, 9, or 10, please). Additionally, this year, FF Resonance has shown a true thirst and appreciation for classic turn-based games on top of the action-combat focus of recent titles, so I’ll be heavily tuned in to see what direction the series goes next.

Check out the full IGN interview for more from Kitase, including his thoughts on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 being heavily inspired by Final Fantasy classics.

Calls for the Canadian government to help ressurect recently shuttered RPG makers BioWare have progressed from a single post by a politician to a petition with enough signatures that it looks set to be presented to the Canadian House of Commons for an official response. So far, 1,662 people from the country of maple syrup and also other things have signed this call for their leaders to consider stepping in.

"BioWare is one of Canada's most important cultural exports to the world in the 21st century, selling tens of millions of units of their video games globally," declares the petition, started by Brendan Routh and authorised by Vancouver Kingsway MP Don Davies.

"BioWare's productions champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights that are at the centre of Canada's national identity," its run of bullet points continues. "BioWare has been shuttered by its American parent company Electronic Arts, now owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners and BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy."

With all of that in mind, the petition calls on the Canadian Government to "provide BioWare with the capital necessary to secure independence of themselves and their intellectual property from Electronic Arts and resume business as an independent, Canadian company". The Canadians who've signed also want their leaders to "protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests" and "champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry".

Thus far, the petition's amassed 1,662 verified signatures from citizens across Canada, putting it above the 500 verified signature threshold required for it to be presented to the country's House of Commons. That'll be followed by the tabling of an official response from the Canadian government.

As with some of the responses from political bodies the likes of the Stop Killing Games campaign have gotten over the years, I find it hard not to see this petition not being greeted with an answer along the lines of 'We do care about this and thank you for raising it, but we're not really gonna do much here'. I think a full BioWare resurrection with government backing is highly unlikely, but finding some way to enshrine the studio's legacy or contribution to Canada's games industry and arts culture seems a lot more easily doable.

A big statue of Blokeshep and Femshep surrounded by their crew of potential allies somewhere in Edmonton, maybe. Or a big stone middle finger that's always required to be aimed at a poster for the next Star Wars film/game/TV show/bit of merch.

Final Fantasy 10's Blitzball was based on The Phantom Menace's Pod Racing

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Final Fantasy series producer Yoshinori Kitase says that Final Fantasy 10's iconic Blitzball minigame was inspired in-part by Pod Racing in Star Wars Episode 1: The Phantom Menace – so he's pleased that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 took inspiration from Square Enix's series, too.

Kitase – who served as game director of Final Fantasy 10 – spoke to IGN about being "very happy" that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was so inspired by Final Fantasy because he himself was inspired by movies he enjoyed when he was young – particularly Star Wars.

"I think I like Star Wars so much that I was afraid of using anything related to [it]," Kitase says, recalling the fear that his work would become something identical to the films. He explains, "I don't think there's something from the movie that I used directly as an inspiration for my games."

However, he does admit to a couple of major inspirations, namely Biggs and Wedge – recurring names used in the series starting with Final Fantasy 6 – who are named after Luke Skywalker's wingmen during the attack on the Death Star in the original Star Wars (Biggs Darklighter and Wedge Antilles). He recalls, "I wasn't sure about the name I was going to use for those characters. And I ended up using the names of characters from Star Wars."

Another major inspiration came when Kitase was creating the fictional sport Blitzball for inclusion in the game. He recalls, "I used an idea from Star Wars Episode 1 where there's this [pod] race and the fact of using sport inside a fantasy context, I took this idea directly from Star Wars."

Frankly, I'm more impressed that he was able to be inspired by a film that released two years earlier, which is a massive reminder of how much quicker sequels to games released, and how on fire Square Enix was at that point. Kitase directed Final Fantasy 8 which released three months before The Phantom Menace, and two years later Final Fantasy 10 – inspired by The Phantom Menace – arrived on shelves.

Final Fantasy 10 leaned into the fantasy genre after devs "learned that The Lord of the Rings was in production" and thought it would be "the next big global trend."

#3884. Country of Fortune release countdown: Exact date and time

Country of Fortune is coming soon to gamers worldwide, and less than 24 hours are left for it to go live. Developed by Nepos Games, Country of Fortune takes city-building to a new level. Instead of constructing your city, you’ll be developing an entire nation, and every decision you make will have a key impact on your legacy.

But first, let’s find out when the upcoming nation-builder goes live.

Country of Fortune goes live worldwide on Thursday, November 5. The release date was announced by the developers earlier, and I am not expecting any change this late. The following countdown will expire once the game goes live.

The countdown is based on the following times.

If there is any change to the schedule ahead of launch, I will duly update it on this guide.

In Country of Fortune, you build an entire medieval country with the use of your settlements. The game uses grids, grows, and knits into a living region filled with people, rivers, and resources.

As a lokator, your first task is to pick a suitable grid to place your first settlement. Then, guide all your villages to help them grow from a hamlet to a bustling city.

Since no two grids are the same, you’ll need to adjust accordingly. There will be plenty of resource deposits to exploit, but you’ll be challenged by the environment and terrain.

With a wide economy, you’ll need to manage plenty of different aspects. Develop settlements and help them specialize in producing goods that require resources from the nearby areas. You can also develop roads and vehicles to set up a booming trade.

With different levels of power and endless micromanagement (if you want), Country of Fortune has plenty of exciting features to offer. If you’re unsure about what to expect, there’s a free demo available on Steam for you to try out ahead of the game’s early access launch.

#3883. You can now play Pillars of Eternity and Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire with a controller on PC from start to finish, thanks to a new update open for testing

Deadfire’s turn-based mode has also gotten a makeover

After gifting Pillars of Eternity a turn-based mode for its tenth anniversary, Obsidian have now rolled out full PC controller support for both the RPG and its younger sibling Pillars of Eternity 2: Deadfire. The support, along with some tweaks to Deadfire's turn-based mode, are currently out in public test form.

"You can now play the whole of either game with a controller, from character creation to the end credits (and, in Deadfire, all the way out to naval combat), in both real-time with pause and turn-based mode," the studio wrote in their announcement of the public test going live. "Deadfire’s support builds on the controller scheme from the console editions. Prefer to switch things up? Pick up your mouse and keyboard at any time, and the game follows right along."

"Deadfire’s turn-based mode has also been reworked with the improvements we made for Pillars of Eternity’s turn-based mode: turns now follow each character’s speed, combat is more lethal, and swapping weapons or drinking potions no longer costs your action. You can now switch turn-based mode on or off during a playthrough, and the update brings a long list of fixes across combat, quests, audio, and the interface."

Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are included in the support, along with the Steam Deck and Steam's Big Picture mode. Radial menus have been worked in to allow rapid firing of abilities, spells, and party commands, with the interface also popping up the right button prompts for your controller of choice.

These additions are all part of Patch 1.3.10.0, the full notes for which can be found in the post I've embedded above, alongside instructions on how to get into the public test. The patch also does things like ensure "the description of Fulvano’s Boots is no longer fragmented". I'm glad Obsidian have saved those soles.

The studio haven't put a concrete end date on the test at this point, instead noting it "will run for some time as we continue to update it in preparation for a full release". As it's a test, those jumping in should expect bugs and other funkiness.

It sorta looks like it's in three dimensions!

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Remember the 3D craze? The Nintendo 3DS, 3D TV, 3D cinema; it was a new, exciting technology that some expected would go mainstream one day. Then the dream just sorta died. People don't talk about it much these days; except for this wonderful project that takes normal videos and turns them, alchemy-like, into slightly more 3D-looking videos using the Steam Frame.

And let me tell you, it's actually pretty good.

It's called framedepth, and it's made by a user going by guix8 on GitHub. It's a plugin for Chrome that adds a stereoscopic 3D effect to any video when viewed via the browser on the Steam Frame.

It's surprisingly fun. I've been watching live gigs and eating challenges on YouTube and the stereoscopic effect is automatically applied once enabled via the extension. It definitely adds some extra level of immersion to it. Not much, but some. I wouldn't go as far to say I felt like I was there in the crowd for either spectacle, and maybe I wouldn't want to be in the firing line of a food challenge, but it's better than I thought it would be. An ever-so-slightly more engaging way to watch YouTube in VR.

The installation process is a bit more involved than your average Chrome plugin, requiring the Steam Frame to be in developer mode. You need to install Chrome on the Steam Frame, which requires a quick trip to the SteamOS desktop to run the Konsole and install via Flathub (flatpak install com.google.Chrome). Then you have to download framedepth from the GitHub and whack more code in the terminal:

cd ~/Downloads && f=$(ls -v framedepth-*-steamos-arm64.tar.gz | tail -1) && echo "$f" # the newest download

sha256sum -c "$f.sha256" && tar -xzf "$f" && cd "${f%.tar.gz}"

bash install.sh # ~/.local/share/framedepth, user service, extension files

Finally, it needs to be loaded as an extension into Chrome, which also requires developer mode to be enabled for extensions in the browser. Once installed, you can enable the 3D effect and change the settings from a dropdown menu right there in Chrome.

The pop-out slider to the max seems to have the most impact on the 3D effect; the equivalent of cranking the 3DS slider all the way up.

There's a bunch to play around with here, but it's worth a go if you have a Steam Frame. If anything, just to rekindle lost excitement for 3D technologies that never managed to win us all over.

Grand Theft Auto is far from the company's only big hitter

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

With GTA 6 right around the corner, Rockstar Games and its owner Take-Two Interactive will be getting ready to enjoy the fruits of their labor with a massive launch, especially if current pre-order estimates are anything to go by. But GTA isn't Take-Two's only breadwinner – CEO Strauss Zelnick reckons that "we have the best collection" of IP in the games business.

Speaking in a new interview with the Wall Street Journal (below), Zelnick defends the strength of Take-Two's full library, which may be boosted by GTA, but by no means relies on it entirely.

"We have 15 franchises that have each sold at least 5 million units in an individual release," he begins. "I think we have the best collection of owned intellectual property in the video game business, and I think that's reflected in our top line, our bottom line, and our market cap."

He continues: "In addition to Grand Theft Auto, we have Red Dead Redemption, a massive title. It sold over 65 million units in the most recent release. Red Dead Online, Grand Theft Auto Online, we have NBA 2K, which is the second-biggest sports title worldwide – the biggest in North America."

In a quickfire round, Zelnick also lists the likes of Borderlands, BioShock, WWE 2K, and Civilization, as well as mobile hits such as Words with Friends and Empires & Puzzles.

Depending on your personal preferences and biases, you may or may not agree with Zelnick that Take-Two truly has the best bank of IP – others like Nintendo could certainly give the company a run for its money with the likes of Mario, Zelda, and Smash Bros., not to mention its partial ownership of Pokemon. But there's definitely no denying its strength – even with the current highest-rated game of the year, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, out today, it's hard to think of November as anything other than Rockstar's month.

With GTA 6 delays, Take-Two CEO suggests Rockstar didn't want a Cyberpunk 2077 situation: "They had to pull the title after shipping."

#3880. How to get Apex Protocol Gear set in The Division 2

The Apex Protocol Gear set is a new addition to The Division 2, and it’s tied directly to the Echoes of Central Park DLC. The DLC has added a new playable area, and you get new bosses to kill.

These bosses are directly involved in providing you with the equipment pieces, but the job is easier said than done.

For starters, you will need to have access to the Echoes of Central Park DLC. Without it, you will not have access to the new location, which is mandatory for farming this gear set. As of writing, there is no other possible way to get the Apex Protocol gear pieces aside from playing in Central Park.

Once you have access to the location, your next task is to finish the main story campaign. It’s a relatively easy one, and you can also finish it as a beginner. Veterans can bring their Prototype gear, but the bonus effects will be unavailable at this location.

When you finish the campaign, you will learn about the Guardians. They were all former SHD agents who got involved in nefarious activities. This completely metamorphosed them and turned them into the apex predators. To get your gear pieces, you will need to defeat all of them.

There are five of them located all around the map, and you can see their locations on the image above. Head to the marked spot, and you will find the Lair of a Guardian. Once you reach a lair, you will have to deal enough damage to make the Guardian appear.

You will then have a set amount of time to kill the Guardian. As you deal damage, you will have the possibility of receiving the gear pieces as reward loot. The odds are not listed by Ubisoft, but they certainly go up at higher difficulties in my testing.

Hence, playing at Heroic will be the most rewarding thing if you do not mind the challenge and simply want to increase your luck of finding these pieces of gear.

#3879. Goddess of Victory: Nikke's PC launcher suffers potential malware infection, with its publishers suggesting folks who've booted since late September do a security check

A cruel twist for the Shift Up-developed epic shooter RPG of cruel humanity destiny

Goddess of Victory: Nikke, a gacha shooter/RPG developed by Stellar Blade makers Shift Up, has suffered a "security incident" which has seen its PC launcher potentially be infected with third-party malware. Thankfully, it seems a patch to make the launcher safe again has been quickly dished out, but publishers Level Infinite are still advising players who've booted the game up since September 27th to do some security checks.

"We have identified that some files in the NIKKE Windows PC launcher were recently tampered with by a third party, potentially allowing malicious programs to run when the launcher was launched," the developers of the game with anime girls who - judging by the promo art - breast boobily announced yesterday. "As a result, your PCs and account information may have been exposed to security risks.

"We are continuing to investigate the extent of the potential damage and review appropriate response measures. We are also conducting a thorough review of our network security environment, including our CDN, to determine how the PC launcher files were compromised. We will take all necessary precautions to prevent further damage and ensure that this issue does not happen again. We deeply regret that this security incident has caused Commanders significant concern and distress, when our responsibility should have been to provide a safe gaming environment."

In order to try and help players "scan for and remove the malicious programs distributed in this incident", publishers Level Infinite have added a feature to Nikke's official PC client that does just that. They're advising that anyone who's booted up the game at least once after September 27th at 15:41 (UTC+9) use that or perform a manual security check.

Once that's done, affected players are advised to change the passwords for any accounts they've used on the PC they used to boot the launcher, as well as generate new API keys and access tokens. "We take very seriously the possibility that this incident may have affected not only your gaming experience but also your PC, accounts with external services, and personal assets," Level Infinite added. "If you believe you may have been affected by this issue or suffered from any loss, please contact our customer support team. We will review each inquiry carefully and respond as promptly as possible."

Going forwards, they plan to improve their monitoring "so that any unauthorized file modifications or security threats can be detected early and addressed promptly", as well as "establish an integrity verification system for external resources accessed by the PC launcher" and ensure the launcher only requires "the minimum permissions necessary".

Here's hoping the studio are able to keep things more secure in the future and that affected players are able to get rid of any malware with minimal suffering or inconvenience.

"Right now you can still buy goods, they're just expensive. In a little while, you may not be able to buy goods at all."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

You may well be sick of reading about it—I am certainly sick to my stomach writing about it—but here's another doom-filled prophecy about the continuing memory crisis. Doesn't seem quite so funny calling it a RAMpocalypse now. The CEO of memory module maker TeamGroup, Chen Ching, is claiming we still haven't seen the worst of the supply crisis, and that even in 2027 "there will be no downward price trend whatsoever."

According to a report from BigGo Finance, which cropped up while I was searching for a credible source after mydrivers wrote about it, Chen thinks the worst of the shortage will be from now until the middle of next year, and that we're likely to get to a point with DRAM that "even money can't buy goods".

"Right now you can still buy goods, they're just expensive," he says. "In a little while, you may not be able to buy goods at all."

This is all on the back of an earnings call for the company, where it announced record quarterly revenue of NT$10.139 billion (around $308 million), which is an increase of 34% compared with last quarter.

TeamGroup, like most memory manufacturers looking to capitalise on the current crisis, is prioritising where it can get the most cash from, and that comes from selling direct to data centre and enterprise folk, rather than us normies. Just as chatty Sam Altman would like it to be. Fully two thirds of TeamGroup's business is now selling into other businesses, where previously that percentage was just a quarter, with the majority going into the consumer market.

Chen claims its relationships with vendors will help it continue to get inventory, even if it has to pay premium spot prices for it. But he notes that supply will continue to be the big problem, suggesting that supply and demand equilibrium is unlikely to be achieved any time before the second half of 2028, or potentially even later.

And, obviously, that means prices will remain high, or more likely keep rising. "How can prices fall when there's nothing left?" he questions like a good little doom-monger. Good 'ere, innit?

#3877. All Captain Aganmi’s Missing Crew member locations in Queen’s Domain

Queen’s Domain has several difficult quests to complete, and one of them involves finding four lost raiders across the map. All of them belong to Captain Aganmi, and he will task you to find their whereabouts.

In this guide, I will briefly discuss the locations of all four of them so that you can get the quest done easily.

To receive the quest, travel to Aganmi’s Camp in the Ombuer Temple region. Here, you’ll find the captain sitting near a bonfire. After serving his introduction, he will tell you about his crew, and you can begin the quest.

To find the first person, head to the Knight’s Encampment in Isle of Neasied. Take the stairs to the left of the portal and continue heading straight. Keep following the same path, and you will come across the ocean in front of you.

Turn left, take a few steps forward, and you will find a tree with a crew member sitting under it.

You can find the second crew along the path to the Temple, and you’ll need a few air dashes to reach the spot.

Navigate the tough spots with the air dashes and continue past the opening shown on the image above.

From there, you’ll find a broken structure that allows you to travel upwards. Continue past it (don’t go on the structure), and you’ll find the body on a small piece of land.

To find the third crew member, you have to defeat the zone’s boss. You’ll find him near the top of the teleporter. From there, turn right, and continue along the path that goes downwards. Go straight, and you’ll find an opening on the floor. Drop, and you’ll find the crew member.

To reach the final crew member, head to the Cemetery Precipice teleporter at Isle of Neasied. Go past the teleporter, continue straight, and then turn right. You’ll come across the structure shown on the image above.

From there, take the path that goes left, continue straight, turn right, and use an air dash. Again, continue straight, and use a second air dash to jump into the wall opening. There, you’ll find the final missing crew.

#3876. Nvidia ensure unboxing a ludicrously expensive new graphics card isn't limited to real life in these RAM crisis times by releasing a GeForce 8800 GTX unpacking sim

Hey at least the card in this bit of 2006 nostalgia bait has only cost you a virtual arm and leg

In what feels a fairly cheeky move during a time when memory shortages have infamously made it pretty much impossible to buy a decently powerful new graphics card without spending approximately a gazillion pounds/dollars/dollarpounds, Nvidia have decided to put out a Steam demo that allows folks to re-live the feeling of unboxing a ludicrously expensive graphics card in 2006.

The demo, dubbed GeForce 8800 GTX - 20 Years of a Legend, has been developed by Dylan Browne. He previously made Through The Ages, a "real-time high end graphical cinematic that takes us on a nostalgic journey through three of NVIDIA's iconic GPUs" which is also on Steam for reasons.

The GeForce 8800 GTX demo, as you might've guessed, is a tribute to that specific card in the form of a tech demo simulating what it was like to unbox one in a mid-2000s bedroom. Seriously, there's a copy of Crysis on the desk so you know this is the domain of a true devotee to the best graphics available in around 2007.

"Step into a 2006-era PC gaming room, unbox the GeForce 8800 GTX, inspect it up close, and install it in an era-accurate PC tower," the demo's description declares. "Explore nods to GeForce history and hidden easter eggs as DLSS 4.5 with Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, Ray Reconstruction, path tracing, and Mega Geometry bring the nostalgic setting to life. From holding the card to the glow of the monitor, rediscover a moment in PC gaming history - or experience it for the first time!"

As the GeForce 8800 GTX was a top-line card that cost $599 on release in 2006 - about $1,000 in today's money if the online inflation calculator I've just used is on the money - this isn't really a 'we know cards are ludicrously expensive right now, but here's a reminder of when you used to be able to actually afford to unbox one' sort of demo. It is at least a free way to virtually experience having blown a chunk of your savings on something that can render really sexy textures without the existential dread of doing so in real life.

Well, I say that, I've just noticed the minimum requirements for the demo note that you'll need an RTX 4070 card. So, depending on your current setup, this might well be a case of Nvidia offering the chance to render unboxing a card you couldn't afford in 2006 via a card you can't afford in 2026.

Is that about the best we can all hope for in 2026? Probably.

Putting a game up on Steam right now comes with some challenges. For a start, AI has made copycats much more rampant, making it even harder to stand out, and that's after you manage to slowly get approved for release thanks to a gigantic game backlog at Valve. In response to the latter, an ex-higher up at Square Enix believes the platform needs to buck up to fulfill its responsibilities.

In a post on Steam, Valve acknowledges current delays around game approvals and says it's working on ways to speed things up. "We're running a little behind right now and taking up to 12 business days," the company says. "Much of that delay is due to having to re-review games, which isn't great for you or for us."

Jacob Navok, former executive at Square Enix, responded to this news on Twitter. "Steam generates 3x the revenue of Roblox while Roblox has up to 1000x more games released per day than Steam," he says. "Yet Roblox games release in seconds via an automated review system and Steam takes weeks."

Steam generates 3x the revenue of Roblox while Roblox has up to 1000x more games released per day than Steam. Yet Roblox games releases in seconds via an automated review system and Steam takes weeks. The problem is not AI games increasing the number of Steam reviews. This is bullshit being sold to you. The problem is Steam is derelict of its duty. Roblox has invested billions into app review process. When you build a product your assets are uploaded into the system as you are building, so you don't get some sudden rejection at the time of release. They have spent a lot of money on R&D and AI systems that analyze and detect problematic content, and also have appeal systems. Valve takes 30% from you as a developer but has spent nothing to invest into the systems required to handle content reviews. Absolutely shameful.November 4, 2026

This definitely isn't a one-to-one comparison. Roblox projects are made in the game platform itself and it has moderation issues of its own. Automation may be efficient, but it's prone to abuse once bad actors understand what's more likely to get dinged. Also: the firehose of slop that is Roblox is not the model Valve wants to emulate, especially as it actively seeks to control its own slop infestation.

Nonetheless, the point stands that Valve could pump more resources into this aspect of the storefront. "The problem is not AI games increasing the number of Steam reviews. This is bullshit being sold to you," Navok continues. "The problem is Steam is derelict of its duty."

Releases leaning on gen AI are exacerbating existing strain on Steam's systems. The amount of games coming out was steadily increasing even before vibe coding accelerated the amount of games and outright slop getting pushed onto the conveyor belts.

That being said, the solution doesn't seem as simple as Navok makes it out to be in a reply: "Moderation is a solvable problem if they invest billions into it."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Poor Valve, it only generates $20bn a year with 5 people working there," he quips. "The money has to be spent on so many boats they cannot afford to hire a sixth reviewer." Doubling down on the hundreds of millions that Valve cofounder Gabe Newell has spent on yachts, he adds, "Everything for gaben's navy."

More serious is his stance on Valve's resources: "It should invest into proper tooling and humans to do reviews at scale."

This looks to be what Valve is doing, as the company just said it has "spent the last several weeks working to scale our process to match" the spike in games submitted.

Navok points to Roblox's AI-assisted detection systems for mature or problematic content, but - again - the context is fundamentally different because it's one company monitoring assets it has control over, not the same sort of open market. The complexity and variance of the games under review is incomparable.

Navok also notes how much money Valve makes annually compared to the issues it's facing. "Valve takes 30% from you as a developer but has spent nothing to invest into the systems required to handle content reviews. Absolutely shameful," he concludes.

When you have small teams facing ripoffs before their game's even out, it's hard to argue that Steam has a problem. But ripoff capital Roblox isn't a convincing North Star.

Becoming Roblox appears to be the opposite of Valve's plan, so pruning or automating reviews so thoroughly that games are cleared in seconds (read: not actually reviewed) might address the quantity issue, but not the quality one many people on both sides certainly seem to care about.

Metal Gear creator Hideo Kojima says he'll be dead by then, but worries AI will eventually "play a key role" in creative fields: "Getting a finished picture is not what’s fun about drawing"

#3874. Nintendo tried adding fast travel to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, before devs realised "we were missing out on the moments of discovery"

"I thought we needed to address this in this new version."

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is being wrapped up in all kinds of modern touches for its imminent Nintendo Switch 2 remake (that owl seems to be less chatty, for starters), but there's at least one quality-of-life feature borrowed from Breath of the Wild that the developers felt was better left on the cutting room floor: fast travel.

In Nintendo's latest Ask The Developer blog post, long-time series producer Eiji Aonuma explained that he initially asked the game's remakers to add warp points so players could get around Hyrule without having to spam rolls and presumably make Link violently ill in the process. But he and the team quickly realised fast travel doesn't work so well in a game that's still, in its bones, almost three decades old.

"In The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, there are many warp points that enable players to move quickly around the game's vast world. In the original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, you could get around a bit faster by spamming forward roll, so I think a lot of players spent their time doggedly rolling across Hyrule Field whenever they needed to be somewhere in a hurry," Aonuma said.

"I thought we needed to address this in this new version. So I asked the team to add warp points that didn't exist in the original game, giving players access to shortcuts. But when we actually tried playing the game with those warp points, we realized that we were missing out on the moments of discovery that came from stopping along the way and wondering, 'Wait, what's this?' Through this development process, we were reminded once again just how important those moments are to the very structure of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. So even though I was the one who proposed adding warp points, they just weren't working for me in the end, so I got the team to take them all back out again."

There you have it. No fast-travel points in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's remake, and it sounds like it's for the best. I avoided warping around Breath of the Wild's open world for the same reasons Aonuma laid out - spotting something odd way in the distance, slowly finding a way to reach it, and then discovering a funky little Korok seed was always a thrill that wouldn't have been possible by cutting out the trek in between main objectives.

Talking about why Nintendo chose to revive Ocarina of Time now, Aonuma said some of the younger developers on the team had maybe never played the original game 28 years ago, and remaking it could "trigger new insights that they can carry forward into future development."

As for the remake's somewhat divisive art style, art director Aya Shida said the team "used phrases like 'a puppet-show feel' and 'the analog feel of practical effects films'" early on in production. "Neither puppet shows nor practical effects films reproduce reality exactly as it is. Even so, both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds," Shida continued.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time comes out on the 5th of November. After getting some hands-on time with the revival, Lottie thought it was shaping up to be a brilliant remake.

#3873. Beyond Nen Hunter Exam Guide & How to Get Nen

Become a Hunter and unlock your Nen abilities!

Before attempting the Hunter Exam to activate your Nen make sure you’ve farmed a good weapon, have some decent skills and are on an appropriate server for good ping since there will be PVP matches. I recommend playing through the Hunter Exam with a friend via voice comms since it makes Stage III drastically easier. Here’s how to complete the Hunter Exam and how to get Nen abilities in Beyond Nen.

Before you can unlock Nen in Beyond Nen you have to complete the Hunter Exam which you can join via the lobby from the Main Menu. This is where you can invite friends if you’re not going solo. The First Stage is The Stamina Race and it isn’t necessarily a race since you don’t have to be first but simply finish the obstacle course by reaching the end in time. Here are some notes:

The second stage of the Hunter Exam is the Trick Tower where the first part is an easy labyrinth with traps and the second is mini-boss fight. In terms of the labyrinth:

The second part is an NPC fight which is fairly straightforward. You just need to practice blocks, parries and dodges as you DPS with for your M1+uppercut combos and skills. Use air attacks to close the distance. Dodge backwards when he’s about to do his fire tornado skill and overall try to zone him with your M1s.

The Zevil Island stage is an open zone PVP match where you need to survive until the end with 2 badges. You have your own and you need to grip a player for one of theirs and just run and play defensively with 2 until the timer runs out (Skateboard or Jump slide for more speed). This is your first real skill-check and if you’re feeling confident with your ping and parries try to isolate a player for a 1v1:

Don’t Grip Players Without a Badge: If you got a badge from a player and they attack you to get their badge back, either run or down them again but don’t grip them. Just run away after downing them since this gives you plenty of time to retreat as they recover. If you grip a badge-less player you don’t get anything and they’ll just instantly recover and attack you again.

Co-op Makes This a Breeze: I highly recommend doing Zevil Island with a friend or two for an easier time via voice comms. It makes it much easier since you can coordinate to find each other and then gank players for an easy badge grip for you and your friend. Then it’s also much easier to go on the defensive with multiple people once all of you have 2 badges.

The last stage is just a simple 1v1 against a random player in the lobby. Make sure you have good ping and follow the 1v1 tips from the Zevil Island section above. Defeating that player will get you your Hunter’s License thus successfully completing the Hunter Exam and becoming a Hunter with a special mark in the top right. This now allows you to get Nen abilities in Beyond Nen by finishing a short quest (more on that below). Note that if you’ve played with a friend up until now they might be matched against you so you can either 1v1 for real or ask to grip them and then help them out in return later.

After finishing the Hunter Exam and becoming a Hunter, you can activate your Nen via Rohan’s quest (The Librarian in Port Town sends you to him) by going and talking to him at Wayfarer Island in the Nen Cave. Simply press P, hide all trackers and then select only the “Active Quest” tracker and follow the “Activate Nen” prompt. Buy a Meditation Mat from the Merchant in Port Town before you go since you’ll need it for the quest. Once you reach Rohan, talk to him and follow the dialogue to activate your Nen. Rohan will then give you the meditation quest:

That’s it for my guide on how to complete the Hunter Exam and unlock your Nen ability in Beyond Nen. Check out our Beyond Nen codes for free goodies to speed up progression.

#3872. Apex Legends adds a grumpy, teamwiping Godzilla to its growing history of unappealing crossovers

No doubt eager as peas to help pay off EA's billions in debt, battle royale shooter Apex Legends is set to run another of its intellectual propertytastic crossover events. This one, starting on November 10th, stars Godzilla, of Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla vs. Kong, Godzilla (1954), Godzilla 2000: Millennium, Godzilla (1998), Son of Godzilla, and Godzilla (2014). I might be missing some.

Besides a profitable range of weapon and character skins, most of which appear to have hot glue gunned an 70-year film franchise's worth of dorsal fins all over themselves, the King of the Monsters himself will show up on the game's Storm Point map. He does at least have more than a background cameo: he'll occasionally blast an area with Legend-melting atomic breath, though brave souls who risk the danger zone can score a custom Devotion LMG with a unique heat ray attack of its own.

Worth noting also that the character skins are each based on a certain 'zilla movie, though as our freelance news writer and associate Large Lizard Cinema expert Ashley isn't working today, I'm not sure which of these are from hits and which are the duds. Walking wallhack motherfucker Bloodhound gets the newest fashion, their skin being inspired by Minus Zero, while my personal favourite Scottish scientist Horizon gets duds based on Big G in Godzilla vs. Destoroyah. Octane's skin is taken from... something called a Jet Jaguar? Google suggests this may in fact be elite Godzilla knowledge, something I clearly lack.

Regardless, and with the understanding that a lot of effort goes into these crossovers, I still kinda wish they didn't exist? Even putting aside basic game-playing problems with how, for example, wacky skins interfere with Legend silhouettes – you couldn't pay me to initiate a fight against a full team of near-identical Gundampeople - it's just icky to have an otherwise sharp, smart, at times fiercely competitive battle royale turned into an animated billboard for a few days.

Besides, Apex already has its own kaiju: the sleepy, pacifist Leviathans that innocently wandered into the King's Canyon map for a few of the earlier seasons. I consider these much better Friend Material than Godzilla, on the grounds that they'd only kill you by accident, and it was usually your own fault - by wandering under their briefly raised megahooves - anyway.

Nexus Mods, the world's largest mod site and more or less a second home for anyone who's ever installed a Bethesda game, has new rules regarding AI-generated and AI-assisted mods on its platform. In short, it's taking a Steam-ish approach: no outright bans on AI content, but it's compulsory to disclose where it's been used in your mods, and to what extent.

"An outright ban will not eliminate AI from the modding process but will prevent people from mentioning its use", wrote Nexus owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann in an update yesterday. "We'd prefer the opposite; it should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform".

So, starting yesterday, modders uploading new projects to Nexus will have to tick a box declaring how much AI was used in their work, including promotional materials. They can declare their mods "AI-generated", which is to say mostly produced by AI; "AI assisted", for mods that are mostly human-made with a little LLM assistance on the side; or declare them free of the tech's touch altogether.

"AI assisted" modders will also have to make public explanations as to where and how AI has been used, in addition to the box-ticking. The tags will be shown more prominently—right after adult-content tags.

Meanwhile, Nexus itself is pledging never to use mods to train AI or to sell them to third parties that want to do so. The site is also introducing new permissions that will let authors declare whether they are open to (non-Nexus) parties using their creations for AI use and training, with the default being "Ask Me".

How long does everyone have to get themselves in-line with the new rules? Glad you asked. "We'll also be introducing a 60-day grace period for existing mods to meet the new requirements, giving Mod Authors time to review their mods and make any necessary changes to them. This grace period starts today (3rd November 2026) and ends on 2nd January 2027."

I was a little unsure as to whether the new rules would truly apply to every mod on Nexus. There are a lot of them, after all, and plenty that have long since been abandoned by their original creators. Nevertheless, Nexus tells me that "it applies to every mod uploaded to the site, including ones that were uploaded prior to our announcement and the grace period." So better get your ducks in a row, mod authors.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Anyway, will every modder using AI dutifully hew to these rules? No, but Nexus says it knows that. "While we hope these changes will encourage everyone to disclose their AI usage, to be honest, that’s not going to happen. Additionally, we are putting clear moderation standards in place, enforced with consequences for breaking the rules", says Folmann. We'll see how it all shakes out in the months to come.

#3870. The Borderlands series has sold over 100 million copies, and Gearbox is "cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year"

The Borderlands series has sold more than 100m copies across all games, developer Gearbox Software has announced. No surprise, then - the studio also said it's cooking up "big plans" for the evergreen looter shooter's future.

"The Borderlands franchise has officially crossed 100 million units sold," Gearbox boasted in a blog post published today. "There aren't many franchises that have ever hit that milestone, and we certainly didn't get here on our own. For us, it started with that first Borderlands in 2009, and we've been excited about everyone who has joined us in the Borderlands along the way. Borderlands has always had an incredibly passionate community. We've been through a lot together, and your feedback pushes us to make even greater games."

So, where can Vault Hunters expect to go next? Gearbox just finished up on Borderlands 4's Year One roadmap - which included two new playable characters, two Story Packs and more - and it's now "cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year." There's no concrete information about what that looks like for now, but the studio promised Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges will chug on in the meantime.

"We're also taking a bigger look at the franchise as a whole. Where can we take it next? What characters do you want to spend more time with? What stories deserve a payoff? A huge part of that is listening to you," the studio wrote. "All that said, big plans take time, and we need some room to work. You can trust that we'll talk more when the time is right. Now is your chance to influence what we'll say."

Borderlands 4 itself experienced a "softer" than expected launch, thanks partly to the game's wonky PC performance, though it seems to have been a success in the long run. A promised Switch 2 port was also indefinitely delayed earlier in the year. We haven't heard much about that handheld version since, but Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick did say the team were focusing on getting Borderlands 4 into tip-top shape before trying to bring it elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's Borderlands 4 review, Rick Lane said the shooter bought a "more sensible script and a true open world to its pseudo-cel-shaded gun-show, but these moderate improvements are undermined by frustrating exploration and combat that takes too long to properly shine."

#3869. The Legend of Khiimori's Mongolian Expanse update brings in frosty mountains and scorching deserts that'll require a lot more than a fur coat and a sturdy horse

Another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a new update for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches."

You don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

The buck doesn't stop there with this update though. You'll find a whole host of new wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

It's a nice beefy update with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some big additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

Unlike all other achievements in Potato Please, the game doesn’t provide you with any description for the Unauthorized Passenger challenge. The only way to know about it is to complete the challenge.

Once you know what needs to be done, unlocking the achievement becomes easy. To unlock the achievement, you’ll first need to get the Sack Cableway automation from the available upgrades. It’s an expensive one, and there are several prerequisites. Hence, it’s best to save this achievement for the late game.

The Sack Cableway automatically picks sacks of potatoes when you place them next to it. To complete the achievement, wait for it to pick up a sack of potato. Once it does so, go to the sack and press the E button.

Getting hold of the sack lifts you in the air, and the machine carries you over a distance. This will complete the Unauthorized Passenger achievement.

This is the only way of completing the achievement. If you try to jump on the sack, the Sack Cableway will fail to pick it up. Hence, that’s not going to work.

Even Nintendo fans are starting to slide toward digital

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Nintendo remains the biggest physical media holdout among the big three console manufacturers, as Xbox has spent years centering its business on cloud and Game Pass and PlayStation is making plans to exit physical media entirely. The company's latest financial report confirms that well over a third of the company's software sales are still physical, but the split is slowly starting to favor digital more and more.

60.7% of Nintendo game sales were digital from April through September 2026, the company reports. That's down 6.2% from the same period last year. These numbers are measuring money generated rather than individual unit sales, so Nintendo warns that "the continued weakness of the yen" is a factor, but it also saw "an increase in sales of the downloadable versions of packaged software."

In a smaller, three-month period running from January through March 2026, the proportion of digital sales rose as high as 67.2%, but that's when the Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen re-releases landed, a notable digital-only outlier. The digital proportion has hovered closer to the 50% mark in recent years, but that's clearly starting to change in a more permanent way.

Notably, none of this data includes digital copies of Mario Kart World that are included in Switch 2 bundles, which means that the true proportion of digital game ownership on the platform is even higher.

A recent survey of "premium gamers" suggests that around 30% of console games owned are physical, so Nintendo fans remain a bit of an outlier in their dedication to hard copy media. Still, Nintendo has insisted it has "no plans to ditch physical games" and its dedication to the format has proven an easy marketing win amid the backlash that Sony now faces.

Yes, Nintendo's main Switch cartridge manufacturer is leaving the business – but that's unlikely to affect Switch 2 games

#3866. Yakuza creator's new studio and its debut game Gang of Dragon are no more after losing funding from NetEase

Nagoshi Studio has officially shut down and its first game called Gang of Dragon is seemingly no more, months after publisher NetEase pulled funding from the Yakuza-like project.

Toshihiro Nagoshi (often cited as the creator of the brilliant Yakuza and Like A Dragon game series) opened his new studio in 2021 and announced his next game with a very familiar title almost one year ago. Now, the Tokyo-based developer has closed its doors, as confirmed in the Japanese government gazette Kanpo.

The news comes months after employees were told that the studio's future was at risk due to NetEase's funding cuts. Nagoshi Studio reportedly needed another £33.1 million (about $44.4m at the time) to get Gang of Dragon past the finish line - a paycheck NetEase purportedly didn't want to cough up.

The China-based Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet publisher has been significantly scaling back on international investments these past few years. Visions of Mana developer Ouka Studios was shut down just after launching its gorgeous action game, Worlds Untold (a studio formed by Mass Effect veteran Mac Walters) had to pause operations to find a new partner, and Halo Infinite lead Jerry Hook's studio also ran into very similar issues last year.

Some developers have been a little luckier. Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture saved itself with a management buyout and now operates as an independent developer, for one.

Not much is known about Gang of Dragon, but its debut trailer featured the violent crime and high drama you'd expect from Nagoshi's previous work. The game also starred Ma Dong-seok, the acclaimed actor you might recognise from films such as Train to Busan and Marvel's Eternals.

"I want us to have a happy ending. I want us to go out on our terms."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

New Blood Interactive has been around for more than a decade—it's celebrating its 12 year anniversary, in fact—and is still going strong. Dusk, Gloomwood, Amid Evil, Fallen Aces, Ultrakill—it's got an enviable catalogue that continues to grow. But CEO Dave Oshry is still imagining how it might end.

By keeping the studio relatively small, letting everyone work remotely, and not putting all its eggs in a franchise basket and spitting out endless sequels, it's been able to keep doing its thing. And that's the only way Oshry wants it to work.

"If we couldn't be successful doing it this way, I wouldn't want to do it at all," he tells us. "Rather than scrambling to find publisher money or investor money, I'd rather just shut it down and be like, 'We tried, we did our best, we made some cool games, that was it.' And I still want to do that. People are like, 'What's the end look like?' And I'm like, 'In 20 years, we're done. I'm gonna say goodbye, shut it down. Thanks for playing our games. That was fun. I'm gonna go fishing now.'"

Should New Blood start to struggle, Oshry has no interest in selling it to keep it alive. "I'm never gonna sell it. I'm never gonna give it to anybody else. It'll be our time." He'll be content, he says, if people remember its games fondly. "I hope people remember us like their favourite game studios from the '90s or 2000s. Except I don't want us to have the shitty ending like a lot of those studios had, where they got acquired or they went out of business. I want us to have a happy ending. I want us to go out on our terms."

It's a promise that hits a lot harder these days, with so many studios getting gobbled up and then being tossed aside. As October came to a close, EA killed off BioWare after years of mismanagement. 30 years down the drain. Like countless studios that have been acquired by the likes of EA, Microsoft and Embracer, there was no happy ending.

Oshry describes the games industry as "a machine that requires product and labour, and that's not us". Instead, he prefers to think of New Blood as a band.

"Our games are our albums. We tour, we sell merchandise, and everybody plays their part. We're like an orchestra now, actually, more than a band. Because we got a lot of people, and a lot of musically inclined people. We're like the Trans-Siberian Orchestra at this point.

"Eventually the band's gonna get old, and we're gonna get tired, and we're gonna do our retirement tour, and we're gonna call it a day before we get sad. Before we're on stage and people are like, 'Ah, they're getting a little long in the tooth. They can't hit those high notes anymore.' So before that happens, I want to shut it down and enjoy my life."

#3864. After a 16-year long dev period, Faraway, a shooting star arcade game about siphoning the energy of other stars, is out now

Lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I said, game development is a lengthy process.

Looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

As mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

Faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. Sure, arcade games might not be in vogue, I just miss them a bit. In any case, Faraway is available to pick up on Steam right now. Seems like it'll be worth a punt!

A new Assassin's Creed Valhalla patch fittingly named "The Most Requested Update" just dropped, adding a range of features and systems that players have been asking for, including the fabled New Game Plus mode.

Ubisoft shared the news on the PlayStation Blog, which notes that the PS5 Pro version of Assassin's Creed Valhalla now sports PSSR optimizations "to enhance 4K image quality and deliver our Quality mode at 60FPS on PS5 Pro." More detailed patch notes are available on Steam.

New Game Plus is, as is often the case among modern Assassin's Creed fans, a headliner.

"We know this has been a request for ages, and we appreciate your patience," writes Ubisoft, some four years after Valhalla's release. "You can now start your Viking quest all over again after completing the main story of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla.

"To access NG+ you'll have to complete the Holy Day Quest, which is the last quest of the Hamtunscire region. (This is before the true ending of the game but since it is a very big game, we’ve decided to allow you to start NG+ a little bit earlier) Each iteration of NG+ will get progressively harder, offering new challenges to players who want to revisit the Viking Age again and again."

Note that you will have to save the game post-update to unlock the NG+ option.

With NG+ in mind, the cap on gear upgrades has been increased from 13 to 27, and upgrading is now tied to the new mithril resource. "You will need a lot of it," Ubisoft says.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

There's more progression to be had, too. "Extended Progression Mode" adds "a more granular sense of progression," by which Ubisoft means gear upgrades and Runes "increase Power by 1 point" while Masteries "increase Power every 5 skill points."

"This mode is intended to increase the impact of your gear. The challenge is greater, but the reward is great for the mighty," the studio explains.

Runes can also, themselves, be upgraded after today's update, and may reach the new "superior" tier. This, too, requires mithril.

"The second addition to the rune forge is in the engrave page; we’ve added more than 300 available engravable runes, allowing players to engrave all of the perks that have been added since the release of Assassin’s Creed Valhalla, including DLCs and those purchased in the Helix Store," the patch notes add.

For all that gear you're hoarding, Valhalla has also added a Stash inventory. "As we all know, Assassin’s Creed Valhalla is a big game, and it keeps getting bigger each year," Ubisoft reflects. So, the kind folks of Ravensthorpe have installed "a newly installed Stash which, when interacted with, will allow players to store any piece of gear and any rune from their inventory."

The long-awaited update is rounded out by two new achievements for completionists (fully upgrade divine gear, and complete NG+), PSSR 2 support for PS5 Pro, and a long list of balance changes "trying to make dual wielding feel better, improve stat runes as well as balancing skill masteries and their bonuses."

#3861. Ablahshikar is a maximalist, sickos only salvage-survival CRPG about ripping organs out of warships and pawning off strange goods that's now out in early access

I don't know what's going on, and I like it

Sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

Ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

Judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

Truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. If you are one such sicko, then you can pick it up on Steam right here.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

We are back. After a long sojourn to the centre of the self, I return—having completed a journey of discovery where I reflected on what I really wanted from modding GTA 5: my true desires, true capabilities, and where I want to take this whole thing as we walk, together, into the future. I speak to you now of the wisdom I have gained from my vagabond travels, behold:

I've put roving packs of hostile cougars in the game now.

The mod to put loads of cougars in Grand Theft Auto 5 is called Cougars, which is easy to remember, and it boasts "seven special cougar types" and four difficulties. Cougar time is initiated with a tap of the delete key, at which point you may choose either Catnap, Furmidable, Feral, or Catastrophe mode, which I am led to believe affects the volume of the cat hordes dispatched against you and the potency of their armaments.

Naturally, I opted for Catastrophe, kicking off a sort of pseudo-game-show opening where Franklin, Trevor, Michael, and Franklin's celebrity bodyguard were all fleeing angry litters of cats. Then we were off, with me—as Franklin—desperately dodging leaping cougars, some of them armed with heavy machine guns, some wearing body armour, some with traffic cones for reasons known only to God. Then I teleported, and the cougars followed me.

This process continued for a few minutes before I realised that, most likely, I was not going to reach my goal of a private jet waiting on the runway at Los Santos International. I performed a rare purposeful teleport to bring myself home, at which point about 56 quintillion cougars attempted to kill me. I solved this problem with an explosive micro-SMG.

When I boarded the plane, I was told I had won, and a man with a cougar for a head and a parade of dancing regular cougars behind him all congratulated me. I teleported away in the middle of their performance. It is good to be back.

#3859. Days Gone studio's next PlayStation exclusive to be revealed and released in 2027, according to new report

Sony's Bend Studio, perhaps one of its lesser discussed development houses, has apparently been deep in development on its next title. The game is reportedly set to be announced in 2027, and released in the same year.

That's according to MP1st, citing "people aware of what's happening at Bend". Like Days Gone, Bend's next game is in third-person. The title is said to include co-op support, but no live service elements.

The report doesn't say whether the game is based on a new IP or an existing one, but it does state that it's not a sequel to Days Gone. The game is apparently "much further along in development" than we realise, which isn't entirely surprising considering Bend has been quiet for years.

The seven years since the release of Days Gone in 2019 have been tumultuous for Bend Studio. The developer revealed in 2022 its next project is a new IP that "builds upon the open-world systems of Days Gone" and includes multiplayer elements.

Two years later, a job post described a game in development at Bend as a triple-A live service project. That unannounced game was then cancelled in 2025, triggering a wave of layoffs at the studio that took place a few months later. Bend hasn't said a word since then.

It's now clear the studio hopped on its next project following the cancellation of that live service game. Seeing as 2026 is nearly over, we're not likely to be waiting much longer to see that mysterious game unveiled.

#3858. How to complete the Schwarzenegger challenge in BitLife

The latest weekly challenge has landed in BitLife, and this time around, you’re challenged to check off quite a few goals inspired by Arnold Schwarzenegger’s life and career. There’s quite a lot to get done in the Schwarzenegger challenge, with a few tricky goals to check off.

Every challenge you can tackle in BitLife is unique, with lots of tasks you’ve likely never attempted before. If you’re struggling to get through this one, here’s how to complete the Schwarzenegger challenge in BitLife.

There are five key goals to complete in BitLife’s Schwarzenegger challenge:

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

To get started, begin a new life. Choose male as your gender and Austria as your country when creating this life. You also may want to consider rerolling your character until you end up with fairly high looks stats, as this will make your later goal of becoming a famous movie star much more attainable.

The next goal in this trial is to emigrate to the United States. When you’re ready to make this happen, select the Activities tab in the bottom right corner, locate and select the Emigrate option, choose the United States as your desired country, and request approval.

The third goal in this trial is one you should prioritize working on early on, as you must be consistent with it to get it done. This task asks you to go to the gym 40+ years in a row.

To visit the gym, select the Activities tab, find the Mind & Body section, and choose the Gym option. Before you age up each year, make sure you head to the gym at least once. You need to go for 40 years in a row to get this quest done, so consistency is key.

The fourth goal in this challenge is one of the toughest ones, as you now need to work on becoming a famous movie star. To succeed at this task, it’s a good idea to focus on it early on in life, as there’s a lot you can do along the way to make success more likely.

First, try to increase your looks if you don’t have a fairly high score for this stat. Work on tasks listed under the Mind & Body category, or consider getting plastic surgery to try and raise this number.

Proceed through school, and once you’re old enough, apply to college and major in political science to make becoming a governor later on easier. It’s technically possible without this degree, but it’s much easier to get done if you properly prepare for it.

When you’re ready to get a job, look for a job in the acting field, ideally something like a Voiceover Actor or Extra. If you don’t see any available listings, close and reopen the app or age up to get new options to appear.

Once you land a job in the right industry, give it your all. Consistently select the “Work Harder” option, build strong bonds with your co-workers and boss, and otherwise put in all the work you can. Age up, and eventually, your hard work will be recognized, leading to you becoming a full-on actor.

Keep at it for a few more years, and once you get enough promotions and fame from working hard at this profession, you’ll become a famous movie star. Once you’re in the right field, this goal really just takes time, patience, and a bit of luck, so keep at it even if it ends up taking a bit to achieve fame.

The very last goal in this challenge is to become governor. This goal is a tough one to check off, as you must have the Politician Job Pack purchased to get it done. Unfortunately, there’s no way to enter this career without it. You used to be able to join this career for free, but the option to do so was removed.

When you’re ready to get going on this goal, start off with a lower-level position, like a school board director, to get your foot in the door. Then, move on to a higher one, like the mayor. And once you succeed at that, become governor.

To successfully get elected and run, you’ll need lots of money and smarts. Put in a lot of work earlier in life to ensure the process is easier when you do finally reach this point.

If you’re looking for other tasks to tackle after this one, there are loads of challenges available to choose from in the vault. Some good ones to consider are the Mean Girls challenge, the Gold Digger challenge, the Demon Slayer challenge, the Jolene challenge, and the Manic Mother challenge.
