It was a big night for Democrats in the US, as a "blue wave" saw the party retake control of Congress in what CNN called "a stunning blow to Trump." Among the night's big losers is former Halo composer Marty O'Donnell, whose run for Congress ended in a spectacular, crushing defeat—and then a dunk from his congressional opponent that can only be described as brutal.

O'Donnell began his political career in 2024, saying he "never wanted to be a politician" but felt compelled to do so by what he described as the deterioration of the US: "Big tech, big pharma, big media, big whatever—all trying to control big government in Washington DC."

That effort didn't work out so well—he placed fourth in the 2024 Republican primary for Nevada's third congressional district—but he tried again in 2026, this time with the support of US president Donald Trump, which O'Donnell enthusiastically welcomed despite previously calling Trump an "idiot." Well, winds and tides change.

Anyway, O'Donnell won the 2026 Republican primary, and then got in the ring with Susie Lee, the Democrat incumbent who's held the seat since 2019. It did not go well for him.

Hey, that happens sometimes—you think you got it, and then it turns out you don't actually got it at all.

But O'Donnell's Trump-toned campaign, complete with dire warnings about open borders, Marxism and the woke left, accusations of corruption leveled against Lee, embrace of the far-right commentariat, and occasional asides to remind everyone that he's absolutely not mad about being fired by Bungie, did not exactly endear him to his political opponents, or very many other people, really.

So after dismantling O'Donnell, the re-elected Lee—who seemed to largely ignore O'Donnell's rhetoric during the campaign—sent him off into the sunset with this:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Enjoy your retirement @MartyTheElder https://t.co/vH8KwKWrdlNovember 4, 2026

I'm just a bystander on the scene—I'm not even American, much less a Democrat cheerleader. But holy cow. You can see that crater from orbit.

O'Donnell did not take Lee's farewell particularly well, which led to even more smoke in the comments.

I think this is one of those times were you have to just take it on the chin and move along. We'll see how that goes.

#3856. BioWare are gone, but at least you'll be able to watch their final days in a documentary next year and oh wait that's really sad actually

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again."

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

N7 day, the annual celebration of all things Mass Effect, is going to hit a little different this year. Before EA killed BioWare, we might've expected to get a teaser for Mass Effect 5, but because that game is now canceled, well, let's just say the vibes in the RPG community will probably be a little askew on November 7. That said, if you're a merchandise store with a licensing agreement from EA that hasn't expired yet, the vibes are going to be downright celebratory, as the Official BioWare Gear Store, "powered by DPI Merch," has some new and returning Mass Effect goodies it just dug out from BioWare's freshly buried grave.

Most of the merch available on the BioWare store has been around forever, as the storefront has been chugging along all the while, but the hot ticket item for this year's N7 Day is likely to be the replica of the helmet worn by Commander Shepherd in Mass Effect. The helmet was first made available in 2021, but it's available for pre-order again via the BioWare store for, brace yourselves, one hundred and seventy-five big ones, or American dollars.

"The galaxy doesn't wait for the faint of heart, and neither does the Mass Effect N7 Wearable LED Helmet," reads the product description. "This isn't just a collectible — it's a reckoning. Whether you bled Paragon blue or burned Renegade red, your path through the Reaper War is cast in detail that honors every impossible decision you made along the way."

There's a bunch of other stuff on sale for N7 Day including branded clothing and accessories, but it's becoming increasingly hard to write about this incredibly tone-deaf merchandising push while BioWare fans are still mourning the abrupt closure of the studio and former employees scramble to find work in the wake of EA's bloodbath. It's worth noting that it's unclear how much EA is actually involved in sales like this one, as it's all run by DPI Merchandising, but it's a deeply uncomfortable 'celebration' regardless. In fact, I'll go out on a limb and say maybe N7 Day should've just been canceled this year.

Mass Effect can still live on – Baldur's Gate 3 and Fable are proof

#3854. Remedy revenue soars by 226% following release of Control Resonant, the developer's fastest-selling game ever

Remedy - the developer behind the recently released Control Resonant - has released a scorcher of a quarterly financial report. It shows that following Resonant's release in September, the company's revenue surged by 226 percent, bringing in €39.6m in Q3.

This performance was described as "a defining milestone for the company" by CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon. The company reported a €0.6m operating profit this quarter, a fair leap upwards from the €16.4m loss from this time last year.

There are some interesting highlights to this sudden surging performance. For one, the US made up nearly half of Control Resonant's players across PC and console, followed by Chinese-speaking regions and then the UK.

Perhaps most crucially is that nearly half of Control Resonant's players were entirely new to the franchise, with the company stating: "Reaching new players was a key goal for this game, and these early results indicate a growing audience for the franchise and for Remedy."

Control (2019) also saw a bump up in sales thanks to the release of Control Resonant, showing a stronger performance this quarter than the past two quarters this year as well as its comparison period (this quarter last year).

Remedy's CEO now believes the focus for the studio is to "get Resonant into the hands of more players." He continues to say the game has provided a solid foundation for growth as other projects (including the Max Payne 1 & 2 remake) are in the works. In short, things appear to be looking rather good for Remedy.

Control Resonant was an artistically impressive but critically divisive game. While many praised the series' adventure into third person action, some felt it had less of a narrative bite than its predecessor. Nonetheless the game quickly blasted past one million sales after launch.

This massive update promises some exciting additions unlike anything we’ve seen before, so if you’re eager to dive in as soon as it’s possible to do so, you may want to learn about it ahead of time to prepare. Here’s when the Dazzling Decorations update will be released and all the new features it’s bringing to Pokopia.

The Dazzling Decorations update for Pokopia officially launches on Dec. 9. This is a paid add-on for the game that is the second part of the expansion pass that started with Bubbly Basin, so if you previously bought this DLC, you’ll get this update.

A precise launch time for this update hasn’t been shared, and likely won’t be ahead of release. Most Nintendo releases tend to go live at 9am JST, though, and Bubbly Basin did, so there’s a decent chance Dazzling Decorations may launch around 6pm on Aug. 4 if this DLC goes live at 9am JST on Aug. 5. We’ll likely know more closer to release, though.

#3852. Take on a time-manipulating corporation in the very Soul Eater meets Jet Set Radio action roguelite CHRONO PUNK

Plus a little bit of Spider-Man, Devil May Cry and Kingdom Hearts

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

The STJV union says Microsoft imposed hiring freezes at Arkane that resulted in delays and additional expenses, which it then cited as reasons for shutting it down.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"After freezing hiring for 19 months, which artificially caused delays and additional cost, Microsoft now uses those same delays and additional costs as a reason to close down the studio."

France's Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo (STJV) union has accused Microsoft of sabotaging work on Marvel's Blade and then using the inevitable results to justify Arkane's closure.

The union said development of Blade "is going fine," and that the game is on par with Arkane's previous body of work, which includes the Dishonored series, Prey, Deathloop, and the sadly overlooked Dark Messiah of Might and Magic. Despite that, "workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded."

"Microsoft chose to justify the closure on economic reasons," the union wrote. "But Microsoft is actually why those economic reasons even exist. Because after freezing hiring for 19 months, which artificially caused delays and additional cost, Microsoft now uses those same delays and additional costs as a reason to close down the studio."

Closing Arkane would defy "financial logic," the union claimed, as it would likely cost more money than just allowing it to finish Blade—and furthermore, it added, Arkane is profitable—"just not profitable enough for Microsoft."

"Microsoft is responsible for the situation Arkane is in today. Microsoft is responsible for the situation the workers are in today," the union said. "So Microsoft has to take full responsibility here and act accordingly."

While its "dearest wish" is to see Arkane "live on," STJV said the studio's future has to go beyond just completing Blade. And if that's not feasible and Arkane must close, it falls to Microsoft—"the company who decided that Arkane has to shut down"—to take care of the hundreds of lives it has thrown into turmoil. Given Microsoft's essentially limitless resources, the union believes the company has a moral obligation to go beyond the bare minimum required by law: "We will not allow the lives of Arkane Studios' workers to be destroyed without the company paying a fair price."

The union is not aiming low with its demands. First, "to give employees control over the decisions that shape their future" while acquisition negotiations are underway:

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

Should Arkane ultimately be closed, it demands Microsoft "funds commensurate with Microsoft’s status as a corporation" to ensure employees are properly compensated:

Those are big asks, but the union isn't wrong about the resources Microsoft has at its disposal: Microsoft's net income for the first quarter of FY27 was $36.6 billion. Xbox is a small contributor to that total, but it is a part of Microsoft, and that makes it Microsoft's issue to deal with.

For now, the fate of Arkane remains unresolved: The studio fell victim to the most recent round of cuts at Xbox, but a recent report indicated that it might yet find a home with a new owner. I've reached out to Xbox for comment on the STJV union's demands and will update if I receive a reply.

From washed-up golfers to British spies, there's plenty to watch this weekend

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The nights are drawing in, which means there's more time than ever to sit in front of the TV, because who wants to go out when it's drizzly and dark? This week sees a crop of streaming hits return for second seasons, and there's a new Liam Neeson action movie too.

Below you'll find recommendations from Prime Video, Apple TV, Netflix, and MGM+. While we don't have any specific HBO Max or Disney Plus recommendations this week, we do have guides to the best HBO Max shows and the best Disney Plus shows. Happy watching!

British spy series Black Doves is back, with another batch of episodes reuniting undercover operative Helen (Keira Knightley) with her killer best friend Sam (Ben Whishaw). Now wife to the new Prime Minister, Helen is closer to power than ever, but when her handler, Mrs. Reed, goes missing, Sam and Helen team up to find out what happened.

Part of the joy of Black Doves is the revolving door of oddball assassins and spies who cross paths (and usually exchange punches) with Helen or Sam. This season's no different, with One Day's Ambika Mod, Alien: Earth's Babou Ceesay, Control's Sam Riley, Scream star Neve Campbell and Blade Runner 2049's Sylvia Hoeks joining the cast.

Once you've finished your binge, check out our list of the best shows on Netflix.

The second season of Apple TV's Owen Wilson golf comedy puts further strain on the relationship between Wilson's washed-up former pro-golfer, Pryce Cahill, and his student, 18-year-old golf prodigy Santi Wheeler. As Santi wrestles with whether to turn pro, perhaps before he's ready, Cahill makes an unlikely decision: to launch a comeback and attempt to become the oldest person to win the US Open.

Arriving just over a year after season 1, Stick is another under-the-radar Apple TV gem. This latest season adds Pluribus star Rhea Seehorn to the cast as a doctor who helps Cahill get back in shape, and also has a romantic history with the stickman.

Fill out your watchlist with our picks of the best shows on Apple TV.

Stephen King adaptations are ten a penny nowadays, but The Institute shouldn't be overlooked, despite releasing on one of the less-popular streaming services. The story of 12-year-old telekinetic Luke, who's imprisoned in the titular Maine facility, it co-stars Westworld's Ben Barnes and Weeds' Mary-Louise Parker.

Intriguingly, season 2 is venturing into uncharted territory, as season 1 covered the entirety of the events of the book, with Luke out to destroy the Institute once and for all after escaping at the end of season 1. The perfect show to watch after you've finished Carrie.

For more, here's a list of the best shows on Prime Video.

The latest daft Liam Neeson action thriller sees the Taken star hit the road in a distinctive red Ford Mustang Shelby Super Snake GT350 after sort of accidentally killing his ex-wife's abusive boyfriend. Neeson plays Ryan “Fang” Flanagan, a highly decorated Special Forces soldier suffering from PTSD.

Much of the movie involves a cross-country chase, with former Michael Chiklis's Texas State Trooper in pursuit. Flanagan also becomes something of a folk hero after word of his righteous kill spreads, with old comrades like Ving Rhames popping in to assist. Great for a Saturday night switch-your-brain-off movie.

Keep movie night going with our list of the best movies on Prime Video.

#3848. It looks like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 had fewer active players at launch in the US compared to last year's Black Ops 7

It's been speculated for a while that Call of Duty may be losing its lustre. Although we don't have concrete data with detailed statistics for each game released in the last several years, there's an observable trend in player numbers that's hard to ignore.

US market analysis firm Circana published some data showing player engagement with Modern Warfare 4 following its launch, and compared them to those by Black Ops 7.

The data is based on Circana's proprietary Player Engagement Tracker, which tracks player activity in the US across Steam and PlayStation, and worldwide on Xbox. According to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, 19 percent of players on PlayStation played Modern Warfare 4 in the week ending 24th October, compared to 17 percent on Xbox, and 4.2 percent on Steam.

With the exception of Steam, those numbers are down compared to last year's Black Ops 7, which saw 23 percent engagement on PlayStation, 29 percent on Xbox, and a meagre 1.5 percent on Steam during its launch week.

Call of Duty managed to land in the top 10 across all three platforms during the same week ending 24th October, per Circana. In fact, it sat just below Fortnite on PlayStation, which is a decent result.

The large drop in activity on Xbox could be explained by Modern Warfare 4's lack of a day-one release on Game Pass. Black Ops 7 was the second (and last) Call of Duty to launch on Game Pass day-and-date with its premium release. Game Pass availability typically boosts player numbers, though not always sales.

The drop on PlayStation is a little harder to explain, but could be a side effect of the incredibly successful Black Ops 1 & 2 ports released in the summer on PS4 and PS5, which captured lapsed players who may have simply lost interest in modern Call of Duty, regardless of the perceived quality of Modern Warfare 4.

Judging by the data we have access to, such as SteamDB numbers showing Modern Warfare 4's launch compared to Black Ops 7's and other recent releases, there's evidence this year's game perhaps isn't as popular as it could've been.

Indeed, even Activision's tenor when talking about Call of Duty first weekend sales has changed. The publisher issued a single statement following Modern Warfare 4's launch, through Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, which does not even mention the game by name.

"One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40bn in lifetime franchise revenue," Sharma wrote on X. "An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."

Last year's Black Ops 7 post-launch statement sidestepped talk of sales and revenue entirely, insteading praising the "great response to the quality and depth of gameplay in Black Ops 7".

#3847. How to get full Tactical Effectiveness in Football Manager 27

Managing your way to trophies in Football Manager 27 is dependent on how many games you win, and at its heart lies the Tactical Effectiveness system. This is a brand new addition to this year’s title, and as of writing, it has the biggest impact when it comes to deciding match outcomes.

Let’s find out how you can maximize the meter and take it to green.

Tactical Effectiveness is a combination of four different factors, and each one plays a key role. To improve your Tactical Effectiveness, you have to enhance all four contributing factors.

This represents how well your team understands the tactics and instructions that you’re trying to utilize. For example, if the players you’re using aren’t used to the shape of your formation, Tactical Understanding will be poor.

To improve Tactical Understanding, you have to focus seriously on the team’s training. There are eight different training modules available under Tactical Understanding. You’ll want to focus as many schedules as possible on these eight modules.

Until your meter appears in the green, sacrifice all other types of training. Once it reaches the green zone, go for Tactical+Match modules.

This part is relatively easy to understand since you need to play your players in their preferred positions and roles. Pay attention to individual training routines to get their familiarity up if required.

This is where your man-management skills will be important. It’s dependent on how willing a player is to believe in your tactics and commands. Not having sufficient coaching badges, for example, will create problems in this regard.

Next, your relationship with staff members and players will also play a key role. Failing promises or not giving players their required minutes will be things you’ll want to avoid.

Finally, you’ll want to schedule at least one Team Bonding session per week to build up chemistry between your players.

This is one of the most important factors since you can’t control it manually. Instead, your task is to ensure that you have a scout with either Outstanding or Elite Tactical Command.

Next, you’ll want to assign them to the task of providing you with opposition analysis. Make sure that this scout doesn’t have any other assignment (aside from scouting the opposition players).

Here are some simple tips and tricks to follow to improve all four major areas of Tactical Effectiveness.

That’s all you need to do to get your Tactical Effectiveness high. Despite the complex nature of the process, acing it isn’t as difficult as you might think. Moreover, you don’t need to get it to 100%.

Voters across the country opted for nearly every local ballot measure that would curb the rate of data center expansion.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Tuesday, tens of millions of Americans voted in midterm elections to deliver a sweep of generational Democratic victories in federal and state races, reflecting a leftward electoral shift that's being interpreted as a nationwide rejection of Trumpism.

But even as Republican candidates and incumbents suffered defeats in what had traditionally been considered some of the party's most entrenched strongholds, the midterms also issued a stinging rebuke to another major source of voter frustration: Data centers. At nearly every opportunity, Americans voted in favor of local ballot measures to halt, slow, or stymie the pace of data center construction in their communities.

As tracked by Data Centers on the Ballot, across the 47 local midterm elections in the American cities and townships that featured ballot measures on data center construction, voters favored restrictions on the rate of data center expansion in 38 of the 39 completed counts. Of the eight races that remain open, voters supporting additional data center restrictions are leading in all six of the races with only partial reporting. For the two remaining races, no results have yet been posted.

Here's the rundown of the types of measures voters are supporting:

At time of writing, only one ballot measure that would have introduced data center restrictions failed: In Harwood, North Dakota, voters refused an amendment to the city charter that would have required Harwood to commission an independent review before approving new data center construction or expansion.

Aside from that one exception, it's not hard to suss out why so many of those measures have passed. NBC exit polls show that 56% of yesterday's midterm voters considered AI data centers either "crucial" or "a major factor" in their choice of Congress person, with data center opponents driven by concerns of environmental toll, energy costs, noise pollution, and—one must imagine—the upward-spiraling cost of RAM.

Square Enix still recommends 50GB to install the action RPG on Valve's store

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Nier: Automata has received a small update on PC which adds three new language options to the storied action RPG, and somehow it has apparently increased its install size from 50GB to a staggering 366GB.

After seeing chatter online, we confirmed this ourselves. When we tried to reinstall Nier: Automata through Steam, we were told we need 366.56GB of space.

I don't know what happened – what wasn't compressed, what was duplicated, what accidentally got folded in – but Square Enix or Platinum Games have septupled Nier: Automata's hard drive demand. Users speculate that the entire game was mistakenly stapled to the DLC footprints, so duplication might be the most accurate.

Hilariously, the patch notes for the update seemingly responsible could fit on your thumb. "The Steam patch released on November 6th, 2026 includes the following," the update reads. Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Korean are now supported.

Notably absent from these patch notes is anything to the tune of: Also, heads up folks, 600% more content or assets.

Outside of welcome language support, the game is unchanged according to all early analysis. In the Steam discussion for this update, other users have reported a chunky but sensible 8GB download for the patch itself. The storage recommendation on the Steam store page system requirements is also the same: "50 GB available space."

It doesn't look like a nefarious situation, so what the heck happened? What have they been feeding these androids? Were we trying to one-up Phantom Blade Zero's 300GB pre-load? Is director Yoko Taro personally behind this, or is he as confused as we are? It's got to be one of the two. That is a man with two modes: uncontainable chaos and unshakable aloofness.

#3844. Indie game website itch.io expands its AI disclosure filter as 'AI slop' continues to overwhelm Steam and other storefronts

Indie game storefront itch.io has expanded its AI disclosure filters, allowing its users to better separate games made with the controversial technology from those who don't.

This expansion, revealed on its official BlueSky account, includes Itchio's search page which now features a "No AI" box. By ticking this, users can hide any game on the website that features the generative AI disclosure. Games created using generative AI must have this disclosure to be present on the platform, similarly to Steam, although without an option to describe to what extent the tech was used.

This change comes shortly after itch.io also revealed the number of game pages being made on the website each day had doubled in the past two months. And, of course, the number of games downloaded and purchases have not doubled to match this new supply.

itch.io is also facing issues linked to the sheer file size. The storefront has a terms of service policy against AI spam, which it cited shortly after it publicly announced "a couple terabytes of AI slop" had been deleted.

This change comes as the industry as a whole has been clogged with an influx of AI games. Steam Next Fest had a record-breaking number of demo submissions last month. Developers pulled demos in fear of their game being copied, and with Steam saying it's the developer's responsibility to make their games less copyable.

It's an issue that isn't going away any time soon. Even as Claude creator Anthropic has introduced rules preventing unoriginal game clones, alternative AI tools can still be used to create them, and the process of creating games using AI tools will still allow for hastily made, low effort slop. Perhaps filters, like the one itch.io has expanded, is a workable solution to this on-going problem.

#3843. GTA 6 is making over a real-life Miami nightclub into its Vice City counterpart for a whole month

A real life night club in Miami is being made over to resemble its video game counterpart as part of a massive marketing blitz for Grand Theft Auto 6.

Starting tomorrow, E11EVEN Miami will be known as NINE1NINE Vice City, as its known inside of GTA 6. As gamers know, everything in GTA games are inspired by real-life destinations, so the game’s nightclub will be transported to the real world as part of the promotion.

The takeover/makeover includes the real world club’s signage and branding all being changed to NINE1NINE Vice City to reflect how it appears in game. And to celebrate its opening tomorrow night, Flo Rida will be performing (I guess Leo Nida was busy).

“We’re incredibly excited to bring NINE1NINE, the Vice City nightclub inspired by E11EVEN, to life inside our venue,” said Dennis DeGori, concept creator and co-founder of E11EVEN. “E11EVEN was born in Miami, so there’s something especially meaningful about seeing our city’s nightlife reflected in the world of Grand Theft Auto 6’s Vice City. As we always say, all roads lead to E11EVEN, but for this one and for GTA fans everywhere, they lead to NINE1NINE.”

NINE1NINE will last from Nov. 6 to Dec. 6, and on Nov. 20, the club will host a GTA 6 launch party, and “the celebration will feature a special performance, with the artist to be announced soon.” Very fun, very mysterious.

“The experience will also extend beyond the venue,” the release explained. “Real-world versions of vehicles featured in GTA 6 will be displayed, giving fans an up-close look at some of the game’s recognizable vehicles while at the nightclub.”

The highly anticipated game’s takeover of Miami marks some of the most incredible marketing I’ve seen for any game, including in-world billboards popping up all over the city, and the Miami Heat game on Nov. 18 featuring Vice City uniforms, branding, and merch. There will also be a bunch of NINE1NINE-themed merch, too, if you’re into that sort of thing.

GTA 6 launches two weeks from today on Nov. 19.

#3841. COD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ patch has nerfed UAV Towers so you're not immediately visible everywhere you go

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 patches continue, with the latest delivering some big changes to the game's extraction mode DMZ. The latest hotfix introduced a key balance change to one of DMZ's most controversial mechanics: UAV Towers.

UAV Towers, previously guaranteed to spawn in every Point of Interest (POI) in the map, have now had their spawn logic randomised. Infinity Ward also reduced their spawn rate by 40 percent, meaning you're less likely to find them across the various regions of the map. As noted in the patch notes, that change also prevents multiple towers from spawning the same area. The only exception is the Deadtown area, which factors into DMZ Order progression and requires multiple towers.

By taking away the guarantee that each POI will have at least one UAV Tower, the patch removes one of the core tactics PvP-inclined and aggressive players have been relying on since DMZ's launch. It's common for players to spawn in, and immediately run around activating as many UAV Towers as possible to reveal the movement of enemy players, even if they're not interested in directly engaging them.

Indeed, some of the UAV Towers cover extraction areas, so it's easy for players intending to ruin the day of others as they're extracting to set up elaborate traps. Making matters worse, a particular character trait prevents UAV Towers from expiring, allowing the scans to stay up for the entire match.

Infinity Ward has not commented directly on that trait, but the developer confirmed it's being changed so the Sedative Inhaler - which hides you from UAVs - also works with those trait-upgraded towers, though that change won't arrive until sometime in Season 1.

Finally, today's update further makes it easier to stay undetected by boosting the Sedative Inhaler's duration to 120 seconds, double that of the previous 60, which should help while we wait for larger changes to be implemented.

#3840. No disc, no buy? Not quite: PlayStation reports profits in latest quarterly earnings

It appears the boycotts did not make much of a dent.

Gamers hoping to make a dent in PlayStation’s earnings to persuade Sony to change its mind on ending physical discs will not be pleased with the company’s most recent quarterly earnings.

For the second quarter of the 2027 fiscal year (that’d be July, August, and September), the PlayStation division reported an operating income profit increase of a whopping 83 percent from the same quarter the year prior. And this is in the exact three-month period directly following Sony’s controversial decision that was announced on July 1.

Software sales increased 10 percent, first party sales increases 30 percent, and game & network services climbed nine percent, while PSN’s monthly active users also increased from 119 million to 127 million.

But when it comes to hardware, a big drop: down 35 percent year over year, which is not surprising but also interesting at the same time. The console is near the end of its life-cycle and prices have jumped up, along with the rest of the tech industry, but interest in new consoles ahead of games like Grand Theft Auto 6 and Marvel’s Wolverine (the latter has sold 2.4 million copies, Sony announced) has some players looking to buy in now.

It’s been impossible to see any PlayStation or Sony-adjacent post in the past few months without the comment section being flooded with angry gamers posting images and memes saying “no disc, no buy” and hoping for a flip-flop on the company ending physical disc-based games starting in 2028. But, as I’ve said from the beginning, if the company does not see a dent in its profits or bottom line, then nothing is going to change.

As of Sept. 30, Sony says 98 million PS5 consoles have been sold so far. That puts it as the eighth-best-selling console ever, sandwiched between the PS3 and Nintendo Wii, but far behind even the PS4’s 117 million and PS2’s record 160 million.

Still, in light of the latest earnings, Sony says it’s increasing its sales forecast for its gaming division by six percent for the next quarter.

"That is a big number to commit up front"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The organizers and supporters of the growing #SaveMassEffect movement have two stated goals: Get EA to commit to funding more Mass Effect games, or sell or license the IP to another developer. There are more granular achievements already happening with the accumulation of more than 300,000 signatures on Change.org, but the main ambition is right there in the hashtag circulating like a virus online: fans want to save Mass Effect, but unfortunately anyone willing and legally able will need some seriously deep pockets, according to BioWare co-founder Trent Oster.

The cancelation of Mass Effect 5 is one of the great tragedies stemming from EA's abrupt closure of beloved RPG studio BioWare, but some people, including former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah, have suggested EA could sell franchises and license out rights to series like Mass Effect so that they can continue under new leadership. Others have cast doubt on the idea, however, and even if EA were willing to sell, it sounds like there might not be many studios with the money to buy the IP and develop a new Mass Effect.

"The scary component of Mass Effect is the audience is going to want the best of 'AAA' development," Oster says on Twitter, seemingly in response to the #SaveMassEffect movement, which he recently threw his support behind. "Rough ballpark (based on contemporaries) is $200M+. That is a big number to commit up front. There has to be a bigger plan in place for the IP to make the math work."

I love seeing all the energy around #SaveMassEffect I think there is a still a great thesis for a well-funded RPG developer who can deliver. Makes me want to get some of the original band back together.November 4, 2026

As my colleague Jasmine Gould-Wilson points out, games like Baldur's Gate 3 and Fable are proof that IP can make triumphant comebacks in the right circumstances. Wizards of the Coast handed Larian the rights to the D&D IP to make Baldur's Gate 3 and Microsoft tapped Playground Games to make Fable after shutting down original developer Lionhead in 2016, but there's a big difference with Mass Effect, and it rhymes with electronic farts. EA is famous for sitting on long-dormant IP instead of selling it, and it's given little indication that it's willing to make an exception in this case.

However, if EA were to sell the rights to Mass Effect, Oster reckons it wouldn't necessarily cost $200 million to make a new game in the series, provided the IP winds up in the right hands. "That said, I think it can be done well for less than that amount with a disciplined approach and an experienced team," he says. Let the hopium begin.

#3836. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is confirmed, finally getting new trailer and full name, 8 years, 4 months, and 23 days after its reveal

Today, Xbox and Bethesda have finally revealed the name and more information about The Elder Scrolls 6. The game, which we now know carries the subtitle Sentinel, was revealed in a special video that took place today, 3rd November 2026, almost exactly 15 years since the launch of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim and eight years, four months, and 23 days since the first reveal of the title card for The Elder Scrolls 6. That's over 100 months, by the way, or 3067 days, if you want to get specific.

In the trailer, a glimpse of the new game - mostly with some fancy sand physics - before the name, Sentinel, is revealed formally. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate," says a quote in the video, attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

"For 40 years, we've explored new worlds, told unforgettable stories, and gone on incredible adventures together," says a blurb for new video. "From everyone at Bethesda Game Studios, thank you for joining us along this journey, for making these worlds your own, and for inspiring us to keep creating. Here's to 40 more."

This reveal comes after a report last week suggested we'd be seeing more of the highly-anticipated fantasy RPG in November, and which also predicted the name of the game. That report suggested that the title will take place in the Tamriel region of Hammerfell, will touch on the "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts". This trailer seems to confirm all that.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, as a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Notably, the reveal of the game is taking place not six months after Bethesda suffered sweeping job cuts (alongside many other Microsoft-owned studios) as part of Xbox's "reset".

So why has it taken eight years for Bethesda to show us this game? Previously, Skyrim's lead designer Bruce Nesmith noted that the studio and boss Todd Howard felt pressured to reveal the game to the world because "the pitchforks and torches were out". "[...] Todd's opinion - one which I share, by the way - is that the video game industry has short memories," he said in an interview in 2023. "Those companies that start touting their games years ahead of time, actually, you know, they screw themselves. The best time to start talking about it is six months before release." It's worth noting, then, that this is what Bethesda did with Fallout 4.

Does that hint at a timeline for more Sentinel footage being shown soon, and a potentially sooner-than-we-thought release date? Who knows. If we are going to see the game again anytime soon, it's most likely going to be during The Game Awards 2026, which is taking place on 10th December.

Theories that Bethesda is hinting at an earlier launch are already surfacing, and a few of them are pretty good.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Yesterday, after eight years of waiting, Bethesda finally gave The Elder Scrolls 6 a title: Sentinel. It then warned that, after eight years of waiting, more waiting is in store because "it'll be some time before we're ready to share more." Then Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, one of the industry's best-known and most reliable reporters, weighed in, saying the game is "still more than two years away."

Schreier's 'two more years' statement, echoed by Jez Corden of Windows Central, attracted quite a range of comments, not all of them of the polite sort. That led Schreier to Reddit, where he could elaborate on his statement.

Pointing out his record of accurate calls on previous Bethesda releases Fallout 76 and Starfield, Schreier wrote, "I'm a reporter. I am not telling you this because I enjoy watching people get mad about having to wait for sequels to their favorite video games. I am telling you this because it is true, and because my job is to report accurate facts and clear up misinformation. TES6: Sentinel is more than two years away."

Did this clarification calm the roiling waters? Well...

Many of the replies are understanding, grateful, and sympathetic to Schreier's plight, but there are plenty that express doubt or distrust, suggesting that the two year window was pure speculation. Others want to know why Bethesda would drop the title announcement yesterday if the game really is that far out, given that Todd Howard has previously expressed regret about revealing The Elder Scrolls 6 so prematurely in the first place. Why repeat that mistake?

A few optimistic souls are holding onto the dream of a 2027 release that emerged from the reveal trailer for Skyrim on the Nintendo Switch 2:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

And then there are the Elder Scrolls fans operating on a whole different level from the rest of us. Redditor Reacryoum, for instance, thinks Bethesda is leading up to a surprise trailer drop on November 11—that's actually one of the more grounded theories to emerge over the past 24 hours. Casting back to one of Bethesda's old Twitter posts, Jayehemcee speculated that the theme of the game is "time," and that this is all part of the game's marketing. I'm not sure how that one works in practice, frankly, but I respect the ambition.

Minimum-Act-7571 put forth the idea that Bethesda is actually messing with Schreier by intentionally feeding him false information, because it's super mad at him spilling the beans all the time—although they also admitted that it's a "new copium theory," and so perhaps not meant to be taken entirely seriously.

I think the best of the bunch, though, is this one from Any-West7160, who believes the Sentinel title reveal contains the actual release date: November 11, 2027. I don't believe it, but I like it.

Here's the video in question—what do you see in the stars?

The best videogame conspiracy theories are always the most bonkers, but what complicates the situation just a wee little bit for Sentinel is that one such theory was actually correct: The Sentinel subtitle was stashed away in a Starfield easter egg for years before anyone noticed. Maybe it was just a coincidence, sure, but the numbers don't lie, as the saying goes—and those numbers said Sentinel. And they were right!

So there's precedent there, pretty certainly, but it's also a lot easier to drop in a reference to a locked-in-stone game title than it is to do the same with a relatively far-off launch date that's subject to disruption and delays. And as others have pointed out, including Schreier, it's extremely unlikely that anyone is just lying about the far-off release window for a little bit of PR pop: Evasion and word games are one thing, but straight-up dishonesty will leave your credibility in shreds pretty much instantly.

What it all adds up to, ultimately, is this: Two more years of waiting and maybe more, plenty of hopium and copium along the way, and a wise piece of advice from Vanquisher_84 which will almost certainly go unheeded:

2026 games: All the upcoming gamesBest PC games: Our all-time favoritesFree PC games: Freebie festBest FPS games: Finest gunplayBest RPGs: Grand adventuresBest co-op games: Better together

#3834. Upcoming BioWare documentary will showcase the studio’s fateful ‘final days’ with inside access

A documentary film about BioWare is in the works and will release next year, presumably including testimony filmed as the studio was closed a few weeks ago.

Deadline reported this morning that the film titled Massive Effect: The BioWare Story “will document how the Edmonton, Canada-based games company grew from being founded in 1995 by three medical doctors… to selling 100 million copies of its role-playing games” like Mass Effect, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Dragon Age, and Baldur’s Gate.”

Filming for the documentary began two years ago, giving the film crew access to the studio in its final days, and will likely show inside the studio when word came down that EA was shutting it down and canceling development on Mass Effect: Universe.

“When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved,” said BioWare co-founders Ray Muzyka and Greg Zeschuk in a statement. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.”

Deadline’s report said that the documentary is “being planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere” in 2027, and it’s got a long list of special appearances, including Muzyka and Zeschuk, along with BioWare developers like Casey Hudson, Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Commander Shepard voice actress Jennifer Hale, and more.

The film is written and directed by Akash Sherman and co-produced by Canada’s Fennessey Films and Score G Productions, which has worked on projects in the past like Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story, Dolph: Unbreakable, and Inmate #1: The Rise of Danny Trejo.

“The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” added writer and director Sherman. “It’s a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio’s recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction.”

Maya Hawke is the first actor to join the cast of Hasbro's upcoming Magic: The Gathering movie.

At Unreal Fest Tokyoâthe annual Epic Games event targeted at developers using Unreal Engine technologyâthe company took to the stage to share updates about Unreal Engine 6, the somewhat controversial upgrade to its engine that puts a far greater emphasis on AI workflows. While developers have questioned Epic’s plans to remove the engine’s existing workflows in favor of AI assistants, the company doubled down on this, with CEO Tim Sweeney attending the event himself to defend the choice.

Detailing the differences between the current engine and the sixth version due for launch in 2027, Epic insisted on its plans to remove Blueprints from the engine. Blueprints are a workflow system that many developers use to script how characters and events work within a game, and have existed in the engine for multiple decades. Epic promises âAI-assisted migrationâ as it moves away from this and other long-term systems.

Though Sweeney appeared on stage ostensibly to apologize for the decision, he insisted it’s a good thing. âWhile it will be painful at first, subsequent productivity will greatly improve,â the CEO told developers, based on a report of the event from Famitsu. Indeed, according to Sweeney, the use of AI in the engine could increase productivity to up to four times that of development done without AI workflows.

âI believe weâre entering a very interesting era,â Sweeney said in comments made prior to his keynote speech, as reported by Denfaminico Gamer. âMajor shifts are already taking place, especially in game development, and the state of the game economy is also shifting at a fast pace. The driving force to this is the acceleration of almost everything caused by AI tools. A significant gap in competitive ability will grow between those that adopt AI tools and those that donât, and the adoption rate of tools is rising in places like China and South Korea. This trend is unlikely to be reversed.” He continued,

Considering this, we intend to maximize the acceleration of workflows using AI in Unreal Engine and use it to help make games even greater. The very nature of competitiveness in the gaming industry is set to undergo a fundamental shift, and I believe it is crucial that a wider variety of innovations emerge from and develop within Japan.

Recent years have seen more Japanese developers move away from internal engines to using Unreal, including Square Enix and Atlus. At the same time, some developers are cautious about the move, and theÂ  debateÂ on the use of AI tools is unlikely to subside any time soon. Epic Games is clearly set on AI being the future.

#3830. How to produce Huge Nutrifruits in Probably Stolen

While trying to make a living in Probably Stolen, players can unlock the Green Thumb achievement and get a good sum of money at a low cost by producing Huge Nutrifruits.

But as you can already imagine, doing that will require more than just unlocking the Hydroponic System. Here’s how to produce Huge Nutrifruits in Probably Stolen.

You can produce Huge Nutrifruits in Probably Stolen by growing their seeds in a Hydroponic System featuring a bottle of Pure Water infused with a couple of Hydroponic Nutrient Tablets. Just keep in mind that the Pure Water label is only given to containers featuring 99.9% purity.

The Hydroponic System can be acquired via the Retired Farmer Favor (250 Credits), which also gives you two sets of Nutrifruit Seeds and Tablets. It’s also possible to start a run with all the base Hydroponic resources by picking the Hydroponic Farmer specialization.

Upon unlocking the system in any way, an NPC will also begin stopping by your store weekly, offering both extra machinery and a source for both Nutrifruit Seeds and Tablets. The seeds will be pricey and cost around 350 Credits per pack.

Shattered Legends is a six-episode miniseries that will debut later this month.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Neither Critical Role diehards nor Hololive vtuber fans could've predicted that they'd work together to film a new tabletop roleplaying series. Shattered Legends is the product of a collaboration that might sound bizarre at first but makes perfect sense when you consider vtubers are basically just voice actors, like just about everyone else in Critical Role's orbit.

Matt Mercer certainly sees them that way. He tells PC Gamer that filming Shattered Legends with Hololive vtubers gave him a "deeper understanding and appreciation for the skill and talent that each of these performers has." The only challenge, he says, was the technical logistics of filming a show with a mix of humans and 2D anime girls.

The original idea for Shattered Legends, before it even had a name, was a pitch from Nerissa Ravencroft, Hololive's "Demon of Sound" vtuber. A long-time fan of Critical Role, Ravencroft says she could barely believe it when her manager told her they were up for it: "I was in awe for multiple days."

"Growing up, I never had friends or knew anybody who ran a TTRPG campaign, so it’s been a heavy desire to play one for a long time," she says. "I just so happen to be one of the luckiest girls in the world, as I get to play with not only my fellow [Hololive vtubers], but Critical Role!"

Ravencroft took the lead on Hololive's side, creating her own character, working with artists on the visuals and unique vtuber models based on everyone's characters, and helping produce an original song.

The story of Shattered Legends was inspired by Berserk and Soulsborne games. All the vtubers—which includes Ravencroft, Mori Calliope, Gigi Murin, and Shiori Novella—wanted to tell a darker story than fans might've expected. Mercer and Marisha Ray, who played alongside the vtubers, helped them fit it into Critical Role's existing setting Exandria as a self-contained "canon-ish" campaign.

The group will be playing Daggerheart, Critical Role's own fantasy TTRPG. For those unfamiliar with it, Daggerheart eschews D&D's d20 rolling system for two 12-sided dice, one representing your 'hope' and the other your 'fear'. If your hope roll is higher, you can spend a point of it to do something beneficial, but if fear is higher, the GM can use it whenever they want to challenge the players.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Mercer prefers Daggerheart when playing with new players and likes how the narrative dynamics "allow for baked-in tension and release, while also inviting players to collaborate in extremely creative ways."

Ravencroft, who is one of those new players, says she was "a bit intimidated" as someone who normally plays videogames, but found it easy once things got going, especially with Mercer and Ray at the table. "Having Matt as a GM for my first Daggerheart campaign is already crazy enough," she says, "but with an incredibly experienced and talented roleplayer and actress like Marisha, we were truly in the best hands possible."

Although the story fits neatly into six episodes, Mercer says there's "much promise of a wider world for these characters," and that "there's always room to pick up these seeds for future adventures" if people want it.

Shattered Legends will premiere on Ravencroft's YouTube channel in mid-November.

#3828. How to get Pure Water in Probably Stolen

If you are looking to stay on the law’s good side while earning a steady flow of credits in Probably Stolen, netting a steady source of Pure Water is the first step.

But how exactly can you break past the High Quality wall? So you can start production as soon as possible and unlock a quick path to high-end trading, here’s how to produce Pure Water.

You can produce Pure Water in Probably Stolen by purifying a water jug, pitcher, or bottle with a +100% Quality Water Purifier. This is a must, as anything below the rating will stop the machine from reaching the 99.90% purification rate needed for the Pure Water label. You can reach the +100% Quality stat by equipping your purifiers with the right modules.

The time required for the purification will then vary based on the grade of the water used, with Rustwater demanding almost a week and High Quality bottles requiring only a night. To make checking your progress easier, we recommend acquiring an AquaScan, which can also be used to relabel products. The needed Quality modules can be acquired via scavenging and purchased from both Dr. Jackson and random customers.

Read what’s behind the latest news in gaming (with a bit of snark) by subscribing to the Destructoid Checkpoint newsletter!

You can get the Water Purifier in Probably Stolen by purchasing it from specific NPCs for 250/300 Credits. To unlock the traders, either purchase the Water Trading starter kit at Wild’s Network (250 Credits) or start a playthrough with the Water Merchant specialization. The purifier demands a steady Power Source, so make sure to invest in a Recharger as well.

If you want to build a self-sustaining water production system, unlocking the Gutterflow via Gutterflow on Tap is also a must, as it allows you to get a secured water supply at no energy cost. Unlockable at Wild’s Network, the store feature can be installed for 250 Credits and upgraded for an extra 350. It’s also possible to start a run with the Gutterflow unlocked by picking the Working Piper perk (-2).

Now that you know how to build your own Pure Water production station, don’t forget to take a look at all endings in Probably Stolen and how to unlock them.

This November has been a terrific month for the number six, with GTA 6 approaching and The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel finally out in the open. Once GTA 6 is in our hands at last, we'll have to reckon with a strange new world where we're no longer constantly waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto – the kind of alien sensation that Hollow Knight: Silksong players, who practically grieved yearning after so much buildup, are intimately familiar with.

Will The Elder Scrolls 6 step up to the plate as the next [clears throat] Massive Sequel Over a Decade in the Making That Also Has the Number Six in It? Is it going to fill Rockstar's enormous shoes as gaming's white whale?

"No, I don't think it is," says Circana games analyst Mat Piscatella when I mention this idea in passing. "It's a huge game, obviously, but things like Grand Theft Auto, Call of Duty, NBA 2K, these are games that are huge, mass-market appeal titles."

This reflects part of what makes GTA 6 so interesting, not as a game to be played but as an outlier to be observed. Similar to Nintendo, Rockstar can basically do whatever it wants because its loyal audience is big enough. More uniquely, Grand Theft Auto is the type of game that appeals to a huge range of players, from the enthusiasts playing dozens of the best games of 2026 to casual fans who mostly stick to the sports and shooter series that Piscatella mentions.

"They're their own thing," he says. "It's a different set of rules, a different set of expectations. They're gonna do their thing, and they've earned every bit of that, just based on what they've done. Nintendo is its own thing, too. They are unique, and I know people hate that and go, 'They're competing just like everyone else.' They are, but with the IP and their history and how they've developed how they go to market, it is a unique proposition. That's why they can do things other companies can't, and they have a relationship with their players that other platforms don't. These are companies or developers that are doing their own thing, blazing their own trail, and a lot of other people try to follow."

As AAA game development faces cost crises, Rockstar is making the biggest bet of all, and with the most favorable odds imaginable. Nobody else could make a game like GTA 6. For anyone but Rockstar, it would be too big to succeed. "If you want to talk about a big bet, they don't come any bigger than this, and the appetite for big bets like this doesn't exist in many places," says Piscatella.

Even The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, follow-up to one of the most-played RPGs of all time, and handily the most-modded, is in a different weight class. (The Witcher 3 and Skyrim have both sold 65 million copies.)

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Whether you're talking about an Elder Scrolls, a Witcher, a God of War, those are big games but they're nowhere near the scale of an NBA 2K, Call of Duty, or Grand Theft Auto," adds Piscatella. "No shade to them. They're all great games and perform very well. But we're talking about a secondary tier to those real mass-market hit drivers."

It certainly doesn't help that The Elder Scrolls 6 was announced eight years ago, and re-announced this week with a subtitle, yet we still don't even have a screenshot. The game is reportedly looking at a 2029 launch, which would put it 18 years post-Skyrim, so I'm going to need Bethesda to wake me up for the third time when, and only when, it's got some heat.

Thatâs probably why there are so many videos and pictures surfacing from last nightâs midnight launches showing huge lines of people waiting for the game and the elusive Zelda-themed Switch 2 console.

Naturally, people gathered at the Nintendo store in Manhattan for an event organized by Nintendo itself, but there are also videos of people showing up at other brick-and-mortar stores like Best Buy and GameStop. Reader, a confession: each night, before I retire to my chambers, I light a small votive candle. Bowing over it, I clasp my hands and beseech the ghost of Josh Sawyer (who is not dead) to return to the Pillars of Eternity games and add the weirdly-decent gamepad support they got on console to their PC iterations. I am an old man who wants to play them on my Steam Deck, and the existing Steam Input templates don't cut it for me.

My prayers are answered. In an announcement yesterday, Obsidian declared that now is the time of the Pillars of Eternity and Deadfire: Controller Support Public Test. Both PoE 1 and 2 have ongoing Steam betas that will allow you to play with full, start-to-finish controller support. You can opt into them and try the new feature for yourself by visiting each game's properties and opting into their respective November 4 beta versions.

Being betas, they're a touch buggy right now. Indeed, one of Obsidian's very first notices to players in the public test's announcement is "This is a public test, so please expect bugs", but I'm nevertheless impressed by the limited time I've spent mucking around with the games on Steam Deck.

There are a couple of misaligned gamepad prompts, and a very slight amount of awkwardness with the analogue movement, but frankly my main takeaway is 'Dang, it's kind of wild how well these isometric CRPGs adjust to non-keyboard-and-mouse support'. Which, yeah, is how I felt about the console versions too.

The public test runs until November 25, and the devs will use the data gathered to iron out wrinkles like those I just listed for a full release.

It's not all about gamepad support, by the way. Just, you know, mostly. Obsidian also announced patch 1.3.10.0 for PoE 1 and patch 5.1.0.0 for Deadfire. In PoE 1's case, the patch mostly smooths out some minor niggling bugs with the UI and the game's recently implemented turn-based mode.

Deadfire's patch is meatier: that game's older turn-based mode has been rejigged to integrate the improvements from PoE 1's turn-based mode. Characters no longer take a single turn per round (instead, they move as much as their initiative allows), lethality has been greatly increased—that kinda thing.

#3824. How to rob houses and escape cops in ROB RUN

Criminal and cop simulator ROB RUN is now out in early access, and robbing houses is one of the best ways to make money. If you play as a criminal, locked houses provide you with plenty of resources. Trying to rob without few key steps will get you caught (and yes, you lose all your loot).

Thankfully, this guide will make you a master robber, and you’ll be emptying houses in no time.

The first task is to locate a house on the map, and head to the location. While your instincts might tell you to just go bam bam, don’t do that. Instead, go to the side, and you’ll find the alarm. Trying to steal anything without switching off the alarm immediately alert the cops.

Head inside by smashing through the glass doors, and you’ll find NPCs. Typically, every house has two/three NPCs. This is critical: don’t shoot the NPCs, but point your gun towards them. This will scare them, and they will refrain from calling the cops.

Once the NPCs are scared, you can then proceed stealing the items. Some items will be in the open, spread on the table and beds. Other items will be inside the closed spaces like drawers, cabinets, etc.

Loot as many items as you can. Before you go on your adventures, go in with an empty bag since you can loot more items. While looting, make sure to aim at the NPCs routinely. Otherwise, they will call the cops on you.

Once complete, escape the location with your vehicle. Make sure not to hit any other cars while you escape because that will also throw you under suspicion. If you manage to complete the steps perfectly, you’ll be able to loot all houses without alerting the cops.

#3823. Arc Raiders devs say that using generative AI voice acting was necessary as actors "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

CCO states: "We are not in the industry of replacing actors.".

Developers at Embark Studios, the company behind Arc Raiders, have spoken on the use of generative AI voice acting in the extraction shooter. It's argued that the initial use of generative AI line reads was a benefit to the voice actors, as they: "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that".

This comes from a recently released video by Embark, focused on Arc Raider's sound and music. In it, several key members of staff speak on the game's use of generative AI, be it the initial use of it for voice lines, and the gradual replacement of it with human line reads.

Audio director Bence Pajor first spoke about the struggles he ran into at previous studios; how gameplay decisions couldn't be changed because voice lines were already locked in. He describes this as a "true pain", and that it places stress on the writing team, dialogue team, and voice actors who may have scheduling clashes. He said that using reachable voice actors in Stockholm, and using the tools available, made life easier for everyone.

Later in the video, Pajor explained that training data was made with the voice actor's performances. Due to the voice lines being required for each new feature, item, or weapon added into the game, he argues it would be too impractical to record every possible version of a line read. "The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that," Pajor said.

Pajor continues by pointing to Arc Raider's many updates and changes since its release in October 2025, it would be impractical to call in voice actors to record lines every time an altered line read needed to happen. Two voice actors present in the video - Jo Rideout (Shani) and Diana Gardner (Celeste) - also shared their feelings on it. Gardner said it was "freeing" that she could take a job somewhere else, without worrying about cancelling other shoots or projects.

However, Gardner would later speak on the topic of her ownership of Celeste's many lines in the game: "The contract seemed so fair [...] so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' [...] This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Even with these proposed benefits to using AI-powered performances, these voice lines are being replaced. Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg said: "we are not in the industry of replacing voice actors", and acknowledges that immersion-breaking experiences many players had when playing Arc Raiders and hearing these performances. Strandberg and Pajor both admit to understanding the AI critique, and point to the work being done to replace what they can.

"We are not in the industry of replacing actors," said Strandberg. "Actually I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance and give them more space. That's something I'm hoping to give to players over the coming years."

Part of this critique over generative AI's use in Arc Raiders came from reviews, including our own. Embark Studios faced similar pushback for gen-AI voice acting in The Finals, however Arc Raider's popularity while using the technology led Nexon to describe it as a "trojan horse" for gen AI's use in small team game development.

#3820. The CEO In Charge Of GTA 6 Is Very Confused When Asked Why He Doesn’t Have More Hits

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Strauss ZelnickTake Two

In the lead-up to Grand Theft Auto 6‘s release, which analysts expect to be the biggest entertainment launch in history by dollar value, The Wall Street Journal‘s tech conference is wondering why Take-Two, which owns Rockstar Games, doesn’t have more hits. CEO Strauss Zelnick looked as confused as you are.

The question came up in the context of Take-Two’s stock being down nearly 20 percent from its peak late last year. With the gaming publisher about to set records, why are investors so skittish? Zelnick essentially responded by saying he doesn’t count his chickens before they’ve hatched. He believes the fundamentals of the company are strong and will be proven out once GTA 6 is out in the wild. That’s whenÂ The Wall Street Journal‘s deputy media editor, Jessica Toonkel, pressed the executive on the company’s perceived challenges.

Toonkel: Is there a concern? I mean, I think there is a concern that this is your big hit and that you don’t have enough hits in your library.

Toonkel: I mean can you, how do you like, knock that down?

Zelnick: Well look, we have 15 franchises that have each sold at least 5 million in individual releases. I think we have the best collection of owned intellectual property in the video game business and I think that’s reflected in our top line, our bottom line, and our market cap. So, um, I guess the way I respond to it is, like, examine the facts. I don’t know.

I mean, look, we have in addition to Grand Theft Auto, we have Red Dead Redemption, a massive title. It sold over 65 million in the most recent release. Red Dead Online, Grand Theft Auto Online. We have NBA 2K, which is the second biggest sports title worldwide, the biggest in North America. WWE 2K, Bioshock, Borderlands, Civilization, and then on the mobile side, Words with Friends, Empires and Puzzles and Good Poker, and hundreds of other titles. It’s a pretty good story.

The exchange has since gone viral as gamers yuk it up over the seeming absurdity of it and how it plays into stereotypes about mainstream media still not having a clue about gaming. Look, I don’t think it was a completely ridiculous question to ask, even if it could have been framed a little better. No entertainment company wants to be tied to the mast of one single hit, even if it could turn out to be the single biggest ever. It is also true that the rest of Take-Two’s line-up faces some serious questions.

Borderlands 4 and Civilization 7 have not been unblemished, runaway hits the way some past entries in those franchises were. It’s been a decade and 2K still can’t get a new Bioshock out the door. Project Ethos, a live-service multiplayer game that many would struggle to pick out of a line-up, has not been cheap and continues to spin its wheels.

At the same time, many other video game companies and platform holders would love to have Take-Two’s problems. They would, I’m sure, trade all of those other potential headaches for annual money-printing machines like NBA 2K and WWE 2K, as well as the ongoing golden goose that is GTA Online. Two of the top-five best-selling games of all time belong to Take-Two. GTA 6 will probably become the third. Nice work if you can get it.

#3818. Ubisoft and at least two other companies are interested in buying Arkane, according to new report

Arkane Studios, which spent the last several months in limbo following Xbox's decision to divest itself from the studio, has apparently received buyout offers from several bidders.

Arkane was recently given until December to find a buyer and avoid closure, an extension from the previous November deadline, thanks to union efforts. Now, according to a Bloomberg report, a few companies have offered to buy Arkane from Microsoft.

The report names French publisher Ubisoft among at least three companies currently in talks with Microsoft to acquire the French studio. No decision has been made, however. The report also said Xbox considered selling Arkane to its management.

Should any of these offers be accepted, it would mean saving Arkane from closure, potentially saving up to 217 jobs and allowing the team to finish Marvel's Blade, which recent reports suggested is nearing completion. Bloomberg, however, said the game is "expected to be released within the next year or two", so it may not be as close as we think.

Arkane is one of several studios Xbox divested itself from as part of CEO Asha Sharma's big plan to reset the business, which saw over 1,600 job cuts with a further 1,600 to be made by the end of the fiscal year.

Studio divestitures include Psychonauts studio Double Fine, South of Midnight studio Compulsion Games, and State of Decay studio Undead Labs - which have all managed to go independent. Hellblade developer Ninja Theory and Arkane had the biggest question marks hanging over them, with Ninja Theory's fate seemingly the most dire after failing to find a buyer.

Given the December deadline Arkane was granted, we're likely to learn the identity of the studio's new owner in the near future.
