#3790. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Navi actor reprises her role after 28 years, but it was a total accident due to Nintendo's blind auditions

For The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's shiny new remake, Nintendo unintentionally cast the same actor twice - 28 years apart - to deliver Navi's infamous "Heys!" and "Listens!"

The Switch 2's Ocarina of Time makes a pretty substantial change to the N64's Ocarina of Time, released almost three decades prior. There's proper voice acting this time, of course - not just grunts and murmurs and hyahs. But even when retroactively adding new things, Nintendo wanted to ensure the remake's cast matched the original's pretty faithfully, so the developer held blind auditions that eventually paved the way for one actor to reprise their role during Link's adventure.

"We felt that if we were going to improve the graphics so dramatically, the cutscenes needed to be fully voiced to match," director HokWai Ng explained in the most recent Ask The Developer blog. "But at the same time, we knew we shouldn't mess with established perceptions of how certain characters sound based on the original. Navi's "Listen!" is one example. Even someone who's never played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time may have heard it before. We absolutely didn't want to change anything as iconic as that."

To maintain the original's nostalgic sounds and voices, Nintendo held blind auditions with the goal of finding actors who could recreate the "feel of the original game."

Series director Eiji Aonuma recalls that the team wanted to choose actors "based solely on which voices most closely resembled those of the original." And, who woulda guessed? "As fate would have it, one of the actors we selected had actually voiced the same character in the Nintendo 64 version. None of us saw that coming."

The duo didn't outright name which character they're talking about, but fans have long been speculating that Kaori Mizuhashi might be reprising her role as Link's trusty fairy companion Navi - at least, in the Japanese language version. A leaked online video of the game's credits now also confirms that Mizuhashi is back almost three decades later. I suppose it only makes sense that the person who most closely resembles Navi is Navi.

Chris Donlan called the new version an "astonishing remake" in his five-star Eurogamer Ocarina of Time review.

#3789. 007 First Light, One Of 2026’s Biggest Surprises, Will Now Let You Play The First Mission For Free

IO Interactive is offering a new, free way to check out 007 First Light, one of 2026’s best games. A new free Starter Pack is now available that lets players enjoy the first mission of the third-person action game. And if you want to keep playing, First Light is on sale on console and PC.

Earlier this year, 007 First Light arrived on Xbox, PlayStation, and PC. It received positive reviews from critics and fans, with many calling it the best Bond game in a long time. Developed by IOI, the same studio behind the Hitman franchise, First Light isn’t just another standard FPS or third-person action game like many past Bond games. Instead, it lets players explore large maps filled with multiple routes and options as they travel around the world to stop a big, bad threat using their fists, guns, and charm. And now, you can download and play First Light‘s opening mission for free on Xbox and PC, and eventually PS5.

Out now on Xbox and PC, the 007 First Light – Starter Pack features the game’s reimagined origin story of how Bond became the super secret agent we all know today. It’s more than just a tutorial, too, featuring some of the open-ended gameplay and design that I really enjoyed in the rest of the campaign.

While it’s not as expansive as Hitman, I was genuinely surprised by how much flexibility each mission in First Light offered. I definitely recommend that Hitman fans who have been curious about First Light check out the free Starter Pack, as you might be pleasantly surprised by how Hitman-y it feels. And you’ll be able to take your progress and completed challenges forward into the full game if you decide to purchase First Light and keep playing.

The Starter Pack isn’t available yet on PS5, but will be released on November 10. In the meantime, PlayStation Plus Premium members can, starting today, play one hour of FirstÂ Light asÂ part of a separate free trial experience.

And starting today, 007 First Light will be 40 percent off on PC until November 9. On Xbox, the game will be discounted by 40 percent until November 15. And over on PS5, First Light will be 50 percent off from today until November 30. First Light is coming to Switch 2 on March 18 after some delays.

I don't remember the last time I actually took a duster to my own rig. But in my defence, I only recently upgraded my motherboard and that required I remove pretty much everything out of my PC in the process of ripping out an old ASRock mobo I could no longer trust in favour of an Asus. So, that basic action meant that I had cleaned my PC by proxy in the past couple of months, though without actively cleaning it.

Which has me straddling both camps of PC Gamer reader, it seems. Because, while the biggest single majority of readers we polled can't remember when they last cleaned their PC, either, a healthy 45% of readers have actually given their rig a thorough once-over in just the past six months.

Now, I get that you have to change your bedding/towels/pants more often than that, but six months is but a mayfly's daydream in the life of your gaming PC. So, I applaud all of you taking rig maintenance so seriously.

This all came off the back of a recent weekly poll where we asked the question: When did you last dust/clean your gaming PC? Sure, over a quarter of you are living in filth, but I'm still proud of the rest of you.

When did you last dust/clean your gaming PC?

Along with the 26% who can't remember, there are another 14% of readers who haven't lifted a finger to dust their PC in over a year. Then there are the paragons of virtue, the children of the light, the 5% who cleaned their PC only that very day they saw the poll. Blessed ones.

But if you look at the numbers in total, we are a culture in balance. There's a healthy 45% of readers who have cleaned their machines in the past six months, and on the other side another 40% of readers who haven't touched their PC with a duster in over a year, with a 15% fulcrum in the middle who have spent time cleansing their rig in the past 12 months.

Equilibrium is everything, but where do you sit on the cleanliness teeter-totter? And how important is it to you?

#3787. Arkane union says closing the studio "would probably be more expensive" for Xbox than simply finishing Marvel's Blade

"Microsoft based its decision only on stone cold and inhuman logic."

Xbox would probably spend more money shutting down Arkane Lyon than it would trying to finish and release Marvel's Blade, according to a union representing workers from the beloved imsim studio.

In a statement posted to the STJV (Syndicat des travailleureuses du jeu vidéo) website, the French union claimed that development on Marvel's Blade is "going fine" and is shaping up to be on par with Arkane's widely acclaimed gameography. By choosing to part ways with and potentially close the famed studio, the union says Microsoft is "sabotaging the game it funded."

After Xbox's sweeping job cuts and divestments from several first-party studios, Arkane was recently given until December to find a new buyer and ensure its future. Ubisoft Entertainment (Assassin's Creed, Rainbow Six) is reportedly one of the companies interested in buying the studio behind Dishonored, Prey and the upcoming superhero adaptation, though nothing has been finalised yet.

The union also blamed many of the studio's problems on Microsoft - a hiring freeze that lasted more than a year supposedly inflated the game's budget and caused additional internal delays. "Microsoft now use those same delay and additional costs as a reason to close the studio," the statement said.

"Even this closure itself is done against any financial logic, as closing Arkane today would probably be more expensive than finishing the game," it continued. "The truth is that Microsoft based its decision only on stone cold and inhuman logic, in which our lives, projects and dreams are voided, so we can better serve Microsoft's short term financial goals[...] The decision to close Arkane is solely the brutal application of a never-ending search for maximum profit optimization. Arkane is profitable. Just not profitable for Microsoft."

The union's list of demands now asks for employees to be able to have a say in choosing a potential buyer, as well as protections against any layoffs that might happen in the next few years. Should acquisition talks fail, the union claimed that the resources in Microsoft's redundancy package are "outrageously low" - so it's also demanding a redundancy payment of €200,000 per employee and further support.

Arkane's not the only developer reeling from Xbox's cuts. Double Fine (Psychonauts), Compulsion Games (South of Midnight) and Undead Labs (State of Decay) all managed to buy their independence, but had to lay off some staff as a result. It's not looking good for Hellblade developer Ninja Theory, either.

#3786. Teacher Arrested After 'Horseplay' With a Student Got Out of Hand

A high school teacher in South Carolina was arrested after his “horseplay” with a teenage student got out of hand.

The Richland County Sheriff’s Department said that Marlin Roberts was arrested on Wednesday, November 4, and has been charged with third-degree assault, according to WIS.

The incident took place on Wednesday at Spring Valley High School in Columbia, South Carolina. Authorities became aware of the incident when a school resource officer was notified that Roberts, 29, and a 15-year-old student had allegedly gotten into an altercation around 11 a.m.

The sheriff’s department said that they learned Roberts “began to horseplay” with the student. As the two joked around, the student allegedly “jokingly attempted a karate-style kick” at Roberts. However, the student apparently lost their balance and fell to the floor.

Roberts then allegedly grabbed the student by the foot and dragged them across the classroom floor, which caused the student to sustain a scrape. It’s not currently clear if the student sustained any other injuries or how long they were dragged for.

Following the incident, the student and their parents reported what had happened to the school.

Authorities said Roberts was detained and he admitted to assaulting the student while speaking to detectives. Roberts was then taken into custody to Alvin S. Glenn Detention Center. Online records viewed by Us indicate that he is still in custody as of time of publication.

Following Roberts’ arrest, Richland School District Two sent a letter to the parents of Spring Valley High School students. He also confirmed that Roberts had been let go from the school in light of the incident.

It’s not currently clear if Roberts has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Richland County Sheriff’s Department did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

The investigation into the case remains ongoing.

#3785. Valve explains why it's running behind on Steam game approvals, asks developers to perform basic release checks to prevent re-reviews

In the wake of witnessing an unprecedented number of game submissions to Steam over the last few months, Valve has been forced to delay approvals in order to deal with the existing backlog.

Following complaints by game developers on social media and elsewhere, Valve has now responded to explain why it's taking longer to get games approved. The short version: re-reviews are clogging up the system.

"We aim to test every game build in a timely manner, typically within three-five business days," Valve wrote in a Steam post. "However, we're running a little behind right now and taking up to 12 business days. Much of that delay is due to having to re-review games, which isn't great for you or for us."

As Valve explained in the post, games need to be re-reviewed when they're rejected for missing key quality assurance checks. In an effort to make it easier for developers to get it right the first time, Valve updated the Steam release checklist to include new, tighter requirements.

These include a requirement to run the game through Steam for at least five minutes. According to Valve, some of the games submitted have not been played through Steam.

"This means that even if a game runs smoothly when a dev launches their executable directly, they might have missed basic steps that would impact a user installing and playing via Steam," Valve explained.

Valve is also making it a rule to mention whether the game requires common redistributables such as DirectX, Visual C++, .NET, XNA. While Steam can automatically install many common redistributables, it needs to know which ones are needed (if any). There are also new rules about achievement readiness, cloud save detection, and some updates to Steam store page requirements.

"We now surface some of the most common issues we see missed, along with asking for some information to help our reviewers from the start," Valve added. "For example, if your game offers multiple languages and you've indicated that on your store page, we'll ask you to ensure you've included them in your build".

While Valve did not directly name gen-AI as a potential reason for this rise in the number of poor submissions, it's clear the Steam company needs to find a way to deal with the massive number of AI-assisted games.

Valve recently addressed Steam's AI game cloning problem by suggesting developers make their games less copyable. Incidentally, some of the developers whose game approvals are delayed now fear their games will be cloned by others using gen-AI and land a Steam page before the original article has made it out of submission.

#3784. Four Small Changes In The Ocarina Of Time Remake That Zelda Fans Have Found And Aren’t Thrilled About

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has been out for about 11 hours now, and fans who played the original are scouring Nintendoâs Switch 2 version of Hyrule for any changes, big or small, from the source material. The gameâs puppet-inspired look makes everything look equal parts lush and uncanny, but broadly speaking, itâs still the Ocarina of Time you know and love. However, some small changes here and there do stand out for people who have played the game multiple times over the past 28 years, and while some are silly, others are actually tripping up long-time players, myself included.

Some of the changes arenât actually consequential, but theyâre fun to point out and laugh at. In the original, thereâs a notorious scene in which King Zora, the leader of the sea-faring Zora people, scoots out of the way so you can reach the next dungeon. The moment is painfully drawn out, as man can only move his body a few inches at a time, so you sit there for a ridiculously long time while he gets himself situated. In the remake, the scene has been shaved off by about seven seconds.

âThen what’s even the point of playing this game?â a TikTok comment jokes.

âI feel like seven seconds is a fair trade off for the comedy of the camera angle switching up,â another says.

There are some changes that only the sickest among us will find. In the original game, players could find secret rupees at the top of the Castle Town gates by walking up the chains on the drawbridge, but it appears thatâs no longer possible in the remake.

The stuff thatâs really going to affect anyone whoâs played the original game are some of the mechanical changes that even I have struggled with a bit as my decades-old muscle memory keeps tripping me up in the early areas and dungeons. The Ocarina of Time remake adds a manual jump button, whereas the N64 original had Link automatically leap across platforms by running off an edge. Now, if you donât press the button, heâll fall, usually holding onto an edge instead, and you have to actually hit the jump button to get where you need to go. It hasnât resulted in any embarrassing deaths for me yet, but Iâm not the only one whoâs falling down when theyâre supposed to be jumping.

[OoTHD] [Kokiri Forest] Proof that I'm a veteran byu/TrunksSSJ inzelda

This is the kind of change that makes the game harder for veterans while also probably making it feel more natural for newcomers. Itâs one example of the effort Nintendo put into making the game more approachable, and any time that a remake sands away friction that was present in the original game, it leads to conversations about what that friction helped evoke. IGNâs Logan Plant talks about this pretty extensively in his review:

I never get tired of entering a new room, taking out the enemies within, and then figuring out what itâs asking of me, like which block I need to push where or what switch I need to hit next. However, there are a number of small changes that add up to make a big difference in how these dungeons feel to work through, not always for the better. For example, a few locks are now placed on doors closer to their respective keys. This effectively shrinks the explorable space in these moments â if you run into a locked door and donât have the key, there arenât that many rooms it could realistically be in. It doesnât ask you to think about the broader layout quite as much as a result.

I understand taking the opportunity to tone down pain points that people have been getting stuck on for nearly 30 years. But this remake tends to overcorrect: a few rooms that used to have admittedly obscure solutions now contain really obvious ones. In some cases, literal guard rails make sure you donât miss the only possible answer in front of you. Puzzles that require a specific item are oftentimes overly telegraphed. For example, even though the hookshot will latch onto lots of surfaces, several places where you used to have to figure out you needed it have been replaced with the unmistakable hookshot target. This removes some of the required thought: you recognize the symbol, and equip the proper item. This has always been part of Zelda, but itâs exaggerated here.

The Water Temple â which is easily the originalâs most infamous dungeon â has fewer small keys altogether. An easy-to-miss room that used to hold a key is now only required for completionists, which takes a huge moment of discovery off of the critical path. Itâs not like every room has been changed in this way, but there are enough instances that they amount to a noticeable trend, which makes the big Zelda âaha!â moments when you overcome something less frequent and less special.

Many pain points have been toned down, but this remake tends to overcorrect.

âDon’t get me wrong, Iâm enjoying the remake,â a redditor writes on a thread about the gameâs difficulty changes. âBut [it] feels [like] all of the changes make an already easy game way too easy. [The] Fire Temple was especially egregious. I don’t want to post any spoilers. but it’s insane how they’ve highlighted the solution to every puzzle, taken out any puzzle that made you slightly think, and ruined the whole goal of the temple in the first five seconds. Huge changes from the N64 version. The whole first room after the first small key door of the Fire Temple is INSANELY dumbed down.â

I donât think anything is easier, I think itâs less tedious,â another player argues. âFor some reason, I see too many people confuse âtime consumingâ and âdifficult.ââ

Part of this discussion is that, since many people who have an affinity for Ocarina of Time played it when they were young and didnât have immediate access to a YouTube walkthrough to give them a solution, those moments of wandering around a dungeon in search of a solution feel integral to the experience. I just played through the first dungeon this morning and realized that I never really had to stop and think about any of the environmental puzzles, and part of me wondered if this was because I actually remembered everything from back in the day or if it was just an easy first area to get through. Now I think Iâm gonna be paying more attention to whether or not it feels like Ocarina of Time is handing me solutions on a silver platter.

Though there are full playthroughs and clips of the endgame circulating online, the majority of the playerbase is going to be chipping away at Ocarina of Time over the coming days, so Iâm sure there are even more changes, good and bad, for folks to uncover as they play the Switch 2 remake.

#3782. Despite hardware worries and rising costs, Sony says PlayStation 6 development is on track and "progressing as scheduled"

Today, Thursday 5th November, 2026, Sony shared its latest financial results, reporting on the second quarter of financial year 2026 for the company. In a wide-ranging set of statements, we learned that the company's overall profits have been charged by the box office success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and that its annual profit outlook has been raised following a particularly successful quarter.

As for PlayStation, Sony CFO Lin Tao hinted at the status of the PlayStation 6 - not yet named as such - which is currently being worked on in the company's gaming division. She noted that the console is "progressing as scheduled" and that staff are making "solid progress" on the machine (thanks, VGC). Tao also revealed that it's been a strong year for the PS5; total sales for the console have reached 97.9 million, thanks to a further 2.6 million sales throughout July, August and September 2026.

The most interesting bytes of information teased out of this call relate to Tao's claim that Sony has been able to offset the rise in memory costs via cost reductions and price increases, all helped by a yearly operating income boost of 89 percent. Sony notes that it has secured enough memory hardware for its next business year, which helps prepare the ground for PlayStation 6 production which should kick off in earnest next year.

"Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

Tao outlines that Sony is beginning to pivot towards this new platform in terms of both investment and production, and that Sony will "attach great importance to a new platform and make the necessary investments for that." This platform - the as-yet-unofficially-named PS6 - will be announced "at an appropriate time in the future".

This all follows reports that the PS6's memory and storage alone reportedly cost more than $680, and that there is still no hard release date set for the console. In light of the fact that console manufacturing is being heavily impacted by the on-going component shortage, many are expecting the price of the base PS6 to be over $1000. We will have to see what Sony announces over the next year before we know for certain.

#3781. World of Warcraft: Forever is off to a great start with Blizzard's smoothest launch in memory

World of Warcraft: Forever came out last night. Those who stayed up were prepared for the usual from major WoW releases: long queues, disconnects, and server lag. However, save for a few minor hiccups here and there, things went off without a hitch.

Eurogamer can report first-hand that for European players who stayed up from, let's say 11pm - 3:50am last night, the login queues were short and constantly moving. Those who were very keen to get in the moment servers went live ran into unclickable server selection boxes, but backing out and re-joining the short queue fixed this problem swiftly.

Once you got in, there was very little server lag save for a lost spell cast or two, nor were constant random disconnects that would boot you out into the cold (I didn't get disconnected once - a record). As far as WoW launches go, an incredibly smooth first day.

This was acknowledged by World of Warcraft developers, such as executive producer Holly Longdale who wrote on X: "At the risk of jinxing things, so far so goodish which is crazy by itself. The team prepared a lot since the wildness of Beta. And this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built plans and contingencies. They are incredible in my opinion.".

Josh "Aggrend" Greenfield, a senior game designer on World of Warcraft Forever, addressed some minor issues that did pop up. These include a zone population problem: in basic terms the megaservers split players into different shards, and some of these felt a bit empty of players. There was also a quirk with the various big boats and zeppelins dotted around the map, which were busted. Temporary portals were added to provide a workaround.

"Thanks for everyone making this a great, super smooth launch," Greenfield wrote. "I’m going to head home and 'go to sleep' now. Yep, sleeping. Totally not playing WoW Forever until 3am. Nope."

The reaction to this silky smooth launch has some players flabbergasted. "I can't believe how smooth this launch is" is the title of Reddit user Arizhela's post, currently topping the WoW Forever board. They continue: "I fully expected to not be able to play today, but I logged in with no queue and no lag."

Another post, created in the early hours of this morning, is dubbed: "Never take a day off for launch, they said" in which a WoW player regrets not booking some time off from work this week, expecting problems. "You've been finessed son," replied user SnooWalruses3948, while SirePuns shared in the shock: "The advice was sound, but this time around the developers hired a witch I tell you. The code must’ve been witchcraft, the hardware must’ve been blessed by a witch as well."

It is unclear just how well World of Warcraft: Forever's launch was, given the unsocialable and employment-averse release time in the dead of night for us Europeans, but it follows a record-breaking beta period in which many hopped back into the MMO. Impressions from this beta were largely positive, the magic of the old MMO seemingly recaptured.

#3780. Russell Brand’s Sexual Assault and Rape Scandal, Trial: Everything to Know

Russell Brand faced sexual assault, rape and emotional abuse allegations by multiple women ahead of his 2026 trial.

The U.K. newspaper The Times published a bombshell article about the actor and comedian in September 2023, in which four women alleged being sexually assaulted by Brand between the years of 2006 and 2013.

Ahead of the article’s publication — a collaboration with the Channel 4 series Dispatches —Brand denied the “very serious allegations” against him in a video posted via X.

“I’ve received two extremely disturbing letters, or a letter and an email, one from a mainstream media TV company [and] one from a newspaper, listing a litany of extremely egregious and aggressive attacks,” he explained, though did not go into detail about the claims.

Brand noted that his past “promiscuous” relationships were “absolutely, always consensual.” He added: “I was always transparent about that then — almost too transparent. And I’m being transparent about it now as well. And to see that transparency metastasized into something criminal that I absolutely deny makes me question [if] there is another agenda at play?”

Brand went on trial in fall 2026 and was convicted on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

Scroll down for all the details on Russell’s sexual assault scandal and trial:

According to The Sunday Times — the Times’ sister outlet —the allegations against Brand occurred between 2006 and 2013 during his time acting in Hollywood and working as a presenter for BBC Radio 2 and Channel 4. One woman, referred to by the name Alice, accused Brand of being sexually and emotionally abusive towards her throughout their 2006 relationship, during which she was 16 years old and he was 30. She previously reported her claims to Brand’s agent, who put her in touch with his lawyer who shut down her allegations.

Another woman, identified as Nadia, claims Brand raped her in his Los Angeles home in July 2012, after which she received treatment at a rape crisis center. A third woman — Phoebe — also accused Brand of sexually assaulting her while working at his home in 2013.

Following the initial article, the outlet reported that multiple women had come forward with new allegations against Brand, prompting Parliament member Caroline Nokes to call for U.K. and U.S. police to investigate.

“This merits and needs a criminal investigation, because for too long we have seen men — and the perpetrators of these sorts of crimes are almost invariably men — not being held to account for their behaviors and their actions,” she told BBC Radio, according to Time.

The London Metropolitan Police later revealed that they were investigating a 2003 sexual assault investigation that was reported following the publication of The Times’ report.

The Thames Valley Police announced they were joining the investigation in October 2023 after a woman came forward with “new information” regarding a “harassment and stalking” report. According to the BBC, the woman previously reported her allegations several times between 2018 and 2022 but no action was taken against Brand. The comedian previously accused the woman of harassing him in 2017.

In December 2025, the former actor was accused of rape and sexual assault by two other women who alleged they had an encounter with Brand in 2009. Brand pleaded not guilty to both accusations in February 2026 while appearing in a London courtroom.

Brand later told reporters that he felt “blessed,” while photos obtained by Us at the time showed Brand carrying a bible. A hearing is scheduled for March 2026 to decide if the allegations should be included in the preexisting and ongoing case against Brand.

“I don’t mind [the media] using my books and my stand-up to talk about my promiscuous, consensual conduct in the past. What I seriously refute are these very, very serious criminal allegations,” Brand noted in his denial video, which was also uploaded to his YouTube channel. “Also, it’s worth mentioning that there are witnesses whose evidence directly contradicts the narratives that these two mainstream media outlets are trying to construct, apparently, in what seems to me to be a coordinated attack.”

He went on to state that he felt like he was “being attacked” and that he and his team were looking into the claims.

Brand subtly addressed the allegations again in a September 2023 livestream on the streaming platform Rumble. “It appears that apparently independent or at least separate news organizations are collaborating — and I hesitate to use this word — conspiring to control global news narratives in some of the most important stories in the world,” he told fans, according to Deadline.

Hours after news of the misconduct scandal broke, Brand received a standing ovation during a stand-up show at London’s Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre. After the performance, it was announced that the remaining dates of his “Bipolarisation” comedy tour had been postponed.

At the time, Deadline reported that Brand was let go from the Comedy Central series Roast Battle after one season in 2018 following accusations of being a “sexual predator” on set. Days later, the outlet revealed that the BBC and Channel 4 had removed content featuring Brand from their platforms.

“We’ve reviewed the content and made a considered decision to remove some of it, having assessed that it now falls below public expectations,” a BBC spokesperson told Deadline on Tuesday, September 19, adding, “[The BBC] does not ban or remove content when it is a matter of public record unless we have justification for doing so.”

YouTube also took action against Brand by suspending his ability to monetize content on his channel, meaning Brand can no longer earn profits from ads featured in videos.

Amid the scandal, several interviews resurfaced featuring celebrities speaking out against Brand’s previous inappropriate behavior.

His ex-wife, Katy Perry, told Vogue in 2013 that she did not want to publicly detail what led to their 2011 divorce. “I felt a lot of responsibility for it ending, but then I found out the real truth, which I can’t necessarily disclose because I keep it locked in my safe for a rainy day,” she explained. “I let go and I was like: This isn’t because of me; this is beyond me. So I have moved on from that.”

Singer Dannii Minogue — sister of pop star Kylie Minogue — called Brand a “vile predator” following her interview on his former MTV series 1 Leicester Square. “I certainly don’t think he has cured his sex addiction, that’s for sure,” she told The Mirror in 2006. “He wouldn’t take no for an answer.”

She continued: “Throughout the whole interview he kept making shocking remarks that I can’t even repeat,” adding that he also made comments about her “fabulous breasts.”

The BBC (British Broadcasting Corporation) announced via news release in November 2023 that it had received five complaints about “inappropriate behavior” demonstrated by Brand while he was working on its radio shows between 2006 and 2008. Two of the complaints were made between 2006 and 2008. Another complainant contacted the BBC in 2019, while two others came forward after the initial sexual assault allegations against Brand made headlines in September 2023.

The BBC noted that the five complaints involve “allegations of inappropriate conduct in the workplace” including “urinating in bottles in a BBC studio” and “inappropriate use of BBC cars.” Us Weekly has reached out to Brand for comment.

BBC began an inquiry into Brand’s conduct in September 2023 after news broke that several women had accused the actor of sexual assault.

According to the BBC and The Times of London, Brand was reportedly interviewed at a South London police station on November 16, 2023.

“A man in his 40s attended a police station in South London on Thursday 16 November 2023,” the Metropolitan Police shared in a written statement with People on Monday, November 20. “He was interviewed under caution by detectives in relation to three non-recent sexual offenses. Enquiries continue.”

News broke in April 2025 that the comedian was charged with rape, sexual assault and indecent assault based on allegations from four different women between 1999 and 2005.

“We have today authorized the Metropolitan Police to charge Russell Brand with a number of sexual offenses,” a spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said in a statement. “We carefully reviewed the evidence after a police investigation into allegations made following the broadcast of a Channel 4 documentary in September 2023. We have concluded that Russell Brand should be charged with offenses including rape, sexual assault and indecent assault.”

Brand appeared in court in May 2025 and pleaded not guilty to the initial five charges against him. The trial was set to start in June 2026.

The Metropolitan Police confirmed in December 2025 that Brand had been charged with two more counts of rape, one count of of indecent assault and two counts of sexual assault after two more women came forward with allegations against the comedian following an alleged encounter in 2009. He pleaded not guilty to both charges in February 2026.

“The women who have made reports, including those connected to the two new charges, continue to receive support from specially trained officers,” the Metropolitan Police shared in a December 2025 statement, per Deadline. “The Met’s investigation remains ongoing, and detectives urge anyone affected by this case, or anyone with information, to come forward and speak with police.”

Brand is also facing potential criminal charges in the U.S. The Times reported on April 6 that Warner Bros. Discovery had offered to submit hours of outtakes from 2011’s Arthur, which starred Brand as the title character, as evidence in connection with an allegation of sexual assault on the film’s set.

In 2023, both Warner Bros. and Brand were sued by an extra on Arthur, identified in court documents as Jane Doe. Doe accused Brand of exposing himself to cast members before sexually assaulting her in a bathroom. Both Warner Bros. and Brand have denied the allegations.

Per The Times, Warner Bros. Discovery attorney Patrick Lamparello told a New York Supreme Court last week that the company had “some hours of video outtake footage … four or five hours, it could be more, around eight.”

Brand’s lawyer, Mark Cuccaro, said Brand had “reasonable belief criminal prosecution is possible in the U.S. based on allegations tantamount to criminal sexual misconduct occurring in the U.S., of which he has been falsely accused both by this civil plaintiff and several others through the media.”

During an April 2026 appearance on the Megyn Kelly Show, Brand admitted that he once had sex with a 16-year-old when he was 30.

“The plain fact of it is that in Europe and in the United Kingdom, where I’m from, the age of consent is 16. And I did sleep with a 16-year-old when I was 30,” he said at the time. “When I was 30, I was a very different person. I was a lot younger, and I was an immature 30-year-old.”

Brand stressed that the age of consent in the U.K. was 16, further denying any accusations of rape.

“I recognize that my sexual conduct in the past was selfish, and I did not apply enough consideration — barely any, I suppose really — to how that sex was affecting other people,” he added.

Following a two-day deliberation in November 2026, a jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court delivered a verdict on Brand’s case, finding him guilty of four of his seven charges.

He was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Brand was acquitted on two separate counts of rape and one count of an attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial.

“Russell Brand was predatory and used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes,” senior crown prosecutor in the London Rape and Serious Sexual Assault Unit David Roberts said in a statement after court on November 5, 2026. “He was a manipulator with an insatiable desire to get what he wanted regardless of whether consent was given or not.”

Brand, for his part, mouthed, “I’m good, I’m good,” to his defense after the verdict was read, per BBC.

Brand was remanded to custody following the trial and is awaiting sentencing on November 9, 2026.

If you have experienced sexual assault, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673 for confidential support.

Feel gud, not git gud; Phantom Blade Zero's action stands out for the ways it sheds the Souls and Sekiro formulas.

PC Gamer's got your back Our experienced team dedicates many hours to every review, to really get to the heart of what matters most to you. Find out more about how we evaluate games and hardware.

What is it A martial arts action epicRelease date October 28, 2026Expect to pay £49.99/$59.99Publisher S-GameDeveloper S-GameReviewed on Intel Core i5 12400F, Radeon RX 6800 XT, 32GB RAM,Multiplayer NoSteam Deck UnsupportedLink Steam

Ever since I started Phantom Blade Zero, I've had a scene from Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon playing on repeat in my head. It's the sequence when Jen and Shu Lien face-off against each other in the martial arts hall. Jen is wielding the Green Destiny, a sword which can seemingly slice through all other weapons, but as it does, Shu Lien adapts.

She uses blades, spears, hook swords, a metal club, but every weapon she picks up, she immediately wields with martial prowess—it might be a bit of a wuxia trope, but it can't help but encapsulate the experience of playing Phantom Blade Zero. The protagonist, Soul's old comrade, Lei Dang, echoes this sentiment when you meet him: "You truly are a martial prodigy - you can master anything you learn."

In a crowded market of action games often borrowing more from Souls and Sekiro than they rightly should, Phantom Blade Zero sheds these strictures in favour of a martial arts adventure that's more about feeling good than getting good. It's not just the endless array of weapons and Phantom Edges (essentially Sekiro's Shinobi Tools) that Soul wields with effortless martial grace, it's about how the game makes you feel like a master.

Phantom Blade Zero managed to convince me—a Dark Souls veteran with 860 hours in Elden Ring—that perhaps you don't have to struggle against bosses to make them meaningful. Maybe a fight or two is enough when a game is packed full of incredible boss battles, each encounter feels great, and the experience is epic enough to satisfy you that you've seen everything it had to show.

Phantom Blade Zero is really a game for those who revel in action combat and its spectacle, but that's not to say it's super easy—it just has a way of making you feel like you're better than you probably are. During one fight with a drunken swordmaster and his flying blade, I parried and Soul dropped onto his back, grabbed the blade between his feet, then forward flipped, hurling the sword back at the boss. I literally pressed one button to do this.

Not to say it's super easy—it just has a way of making you feel like you're better than you probably are.

There are so many jaw-dropping moments—elaborate parries and executions, or dynamic attacks where Soul automatically engages an entire group of enemies—that basically had me yelling at the screen because I couldn't believe what I'd just pulled off. Like any good kung-fu movie, it's effortlessly stylish, but rather than the all-too-familiar drudgery that can stem from Soulslikes crushing you into the dirt and making you feel your skill level, Phantom Blade Zero more often tries to uplift you, reveling in the roleplay fantasy of a martial master.

It also makes the wuxia genre feel approachable. I'd be the first to admit, even as a westerner relatively familiar with Chinese mythology, I struggled to understand what was happening in Black Myth Wukong a lot of time. By comparison, Phantom Blade is a classic revenge plot. Soul, a martially-gifted orphan of mysterious providence, now outlaw, travels to the town of Pangzhen to confront his sworn brother and betrayer, Zuo Shang, after they stabbed each other through the heart. His replacement, The Tainted Heart, only lasts 66 days, so he has to beat Zuo Shang to the prize, a rumoured artificial heart, hence the top difficulty's fun and loreful limitation of 66 lives.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Though its dialogue is a bit on the nose at times, Phantom Blade does a great job of gradually exposing its ill-fated characters, dark setting, and sorrowful story of martial sects grasping to harness unearthly powers. It also carries forward Black Myth Wukong's tendency to surprise you with cutscenes of different styles, including Chinese shadow puppetry.

Coupled with its dark story, it makes for a far dirtier version of wuxia.

It's most adept at teasing its bosses, though, by telling their stories through found notes and Memory Flower collectibles in each region, or via Dark Souls 3 opening-style cinematics. Coupled with its dark story, it makes for a far dirtier version of wuxia, channeling aspects of kung-fu and wild west cinema as we see roundtables of fated standoffs with tragic foes we're yet to face.

Phantom Blade Zero is demonstrably not a Soulslike—hell, it's even less of one than Black Myth Wukong was. Though it has the recognisable structure of bells (bonfires) and remnant echoes (souls), it does away with almost everything else, much to its benefit.

This makes for an action game with a lot more momentum. Rather than banging your head against the same boss ten times, you might fight three or more bosses in the same period—Phantom Blade clearly understands that the spectacle of boss battles is one of the core pillars of a great action game, so there are a lot of them with varied gimmicks.

The game also takes notes from Sekiro, but mechanically responds to two of its, arguably, most debated issues. Namely:

Attacking, deflecting, and parrying to break a boss's stamina in Phantom Blade doesn't give you a critical attack, but instead grants a period in which they can't block your assault. This encourages experimentation, and ultimately, allows you to style on a boss however you wish for the duration. Being aggressive, versus baiting out parries, is encouraged, since regular attacks don't consume stamina and without crits, you have to progressively deal damage to win the fight.

Familiarising yourself with Phantom Blade's massive array of Phantom Edges (the Shinobi Tool equivalent) is also incentivised, since they use a spark resource you get a set number of anytime you rest, but can also recoup through accessories and skills. I personally used the gigantic Dread Axe to smash opponents, and the Fire Meteor, a brazier of green flame on a chain that you kick around to ignite enemies. There are also shields, bows, throwing knives, cannons, guns, spike balls and chains, bashpoles, and even summon options, to name a few.

What's more, since weapons and Phantom Edges gain new abilities every five levels, (up to 30), and Phantom Blade is extremely generous with upgrade materials, letting you easily refund everything you put into them, you're always experimenting. I feel like it says something that I upgraded four weapons and two Phantom Edges fully in my playthrough, yet still had 3 million remnant echoes and the means to level far more.

Good thing, too, considering I have another 20 weapons and 22 Phantom Edges to master in my New Game+ run.

I only have one chief complaint with Phantom Blade Zero. Though the game is quite large—it took me 50ish hours to do everything and unlock the "true" ending—it's unfortunately rather hand-holdy when it comes to its secrets, meticulously guiding you through the game with an almost exhausting quantity of quests and map markers.

It's unfortunately rather hand-holdy when it comes to its secrets.

Since Phantom Edges can be used to unlock areas in previous regions, it has some Metroidvania qualities, but none of these secrets feel especially significant, or equivalent to, say, what other examples of the genre have accomplished, like finding a secret region or boss in Silksong.

Despite appearances, the game is rather linear due to its quests, map markers, and where it places important progression items. Even its more secret, optional regions, are basically impossible to miss, which is such a shame when the game has multiple endings based upon where you go and what you do. It's a level of handholding that made me fervently wish Phantom Blade had taken more influence from Souls in this department at least, especially as playing regular difficulty sets up New Game+ and its escalating challenge in a really attractive way.

I'm rarely a New Game+ person, but upon finishing Phantom Blade, I immediately started again. The game lets you keep your weapons, Phantom Edges, and accessories, so you have more methods to deal with the now-tougher bosses you encounter earlier in the game.

Still, that alone is not enough to ultimately dampen my sincere enjoyment of Phantom Blade. It's a veritable feast for any lover of action combat and fun boss battles. Its soundtrack, too, is noteworthy, blurring the line between traditional Chinese folk music and modern genres in a way that really compliments the spectacle of every fight. I especially enjoyed the Banyan Tree theme, Asura of Wrath—who doesn't love a bit of throat singing?

The game also runs very well. My relatively humble RX 6800 XT produced decent results. Though I did get some more notable frame dips in certain fights with lots of particle effects going on, such as during heavier rain. But on the whole I am incredibly impressed with Phantom Blade Zero. I enjoyed it significantly more than Black Myth Wukong. Alongside Onimusha, it's definitely one of this year's must-plays for fans of action combat.

Phantom Blade Zero tips: Conquer the WulinPhantom Blade Zero Flesh Lily: Find Yu'er's flowerPhantom Blade Zero Zhang's treasures: Every relicPhantom Blade Zero Mandate Camp Key: Get insidePhantom Blade Zero Illusory Pipa: Repair the lute

Feel gud, not git gud; Phantom Blade Zero's action stands out for the ways it sheds the Souls and Sekiro formulas.

Sean's first PC games were Full Throttle and Total Annihilation and his taste has stayed much the same since. When not scouring games for secrets or bashing his head against puzzles, you'll find him revisiting old Total War campaigns, agonizing over his Destiny 2 fit, or still trying to finish the Horus Heresy. Sean has also written for EDGE, Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, EGMNOW, and Inverse.

#3778. PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine

As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high.

In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year.

Notably, despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed. The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei, meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025.

More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers.

Elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled", with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and says it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform."

It must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the company's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028. It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.

#3775. Nintendo game sales surge thanks to Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, but Switch 2 hardware suffers big decline

Nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down.

As per Nintendo's 2nd Quarter fiscal earnings report, focusing on the three-month period ending 30th September 2026, Switch 2 hardware registered a big drop in sales during the first half of the current financial year (FY27).

Over that period, Nintendo sold 6.49m Switch 2 units and 1.27m units of the original Switch - equating to a 37.4 percent decline for Switch 2 and 32.7 percent decline for Switch 1 compared to the same period last year. Nintendo had previously forecast a decline in hardware sales, and the company still expects to sell 16.50m Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year.

Nintendo software sales, on the other hand, saw a big year-on-year boost of 18.8 percent on Switch 2 (to 24.49m units) and a smaller increase of 6.8 percent on Switch 1. That's all thanks to the release of several popular first- and third-party titles over the first half of FY27. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream was by far the most successful game with 8.81m units sold, followed by Rhythm Heaven Groove at 2.89m. Splatoon Raiders (the only Switch 2 exclusive of the three) sold 2.42m. Nintendo also highlighted a 60.5 percent year-on-year increase in digital game sales.

The increase in software unit sales and the "continued weakness of the Yen" couldn't prevent the overall business from declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year, however.

Other remaining releases in Nintendo' s current fiscal year include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake (which launches today and was awarded five stars in Eurogamer's review), Switch 2 re-releases of Pikmin 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles 3, as well as Metroid Ravenous, which arrives early in 2027.

#3774. Spencer Pratt Reacts to L.A. Mayor Race Results After ‘Humiliation Ritual’

Spencer Pratt isn’t holding back when it comes to his thoughts on Nithya Raman beating Karen Bass to become the next mayor of Los Angeles.

“Nithya didn’t win. Karen lost,” Pratt, 43, wrote via X on Thursday, November 5. “You simply can’t destroy a city as much as she did. She played with fire, and she got fired. Nithya won’t offer any reprieve, though. She’s a moron, and the city will continue to decline. The real loser today is LA, but we were gonna tank with either candidate.”

Earlier in the day, NBC News projected that Raman, 45, will be the next mayor of Los Angeles. The Los Angeles City Council member will lead the city for major events, including the 2028 Olympic Games.

Pratt, who was inspired to run for L.A. Mayor after losing his home due to the Palisades fire but lost in the June primary, believes Bass, 73, didn’t lose the election because of one thing.

“It wasn’t the wildfire that did her in; the Palisades held their nose and voted for her, and the rest of LA doesn’t care about the Palisades. They had their own reasons,” Pratt claimed. “South Central hates Karen cuz she abandoned them in favor of criminal migrants. Boyle Heights hates her for the warehouse fire. DTLA hates her for the bums. Hollywood hates her for the restaurant collapse and water main breaks.”

The former Hills star added, “When Nithya presides over the same intractable issues in LA, they will hate her all the same. LA needed radical change. Not a change in radicals.”

In a statement, Bass thanked all of her supporters and praised Los Angeles for giving her the opportunity to become the first Black woman mayor in the history of the city.

“Thank you, Los Angeles. Serving as your mayor has been the honor of my life,” she wrote via Instagram on Thursday. “To every volunteer, supporter and Angeleno who believed in this work: thank you. The progress we made belongs to all of us. I’ve called Councilmember Raman to congratulate her, and I’m committed to a smooth transition. I love Los Angeles. I believe in Los Angeles. And I will continue to ensure the promise of a better life belongs to all of us.”

Looking towards the future, Pratt made it clear that he is not confident in Raman’s abilities.

“I don’t see Nithya as an ideologue. I see her as a moron. She’s pillow soft and can be bullied,” Pratt claimed via X. “Big voices in LA will be able to bully her into shifting her positions, as she has shown with her constant waffling on every issue. Keep pressure on her, be ruthless and you can mitigate some of the damage she will do.”

During her election night speech held at the Greek Theatre in Los Angeles, Raman said she had “enough of establishment politics.”

“This campaign has made it clear that the days of our broken status quo are over,” she continued, via Politico.

In his latest X post, Pratt had one final thought for those following the race for L.A. Mayor.

“This wasn’t an election…it was a humiliation ritual. Especially for my neighbors in the Palisades, who endured the extra indignity of casting their ballots for the witch who burned down our town, only to see their pick ultimately lose, so it was all for naught,” he said. “Anyway. Take the primaries more seriously from now on, yeah?”

#3773. Woim Is A Super-Smart Puzzle Game That Combines Snake With Stephen’s Sausage Roll

The pantheon of super-cute, super-tough puzzle games can welcome a new member.Â Woim deserves a place alongside the heralded greats of recent years, the likes ofÂ A Monster’s Expedition, A Good Snowman Is Hard to Build,Â andÂ Bonfire Peaks, and yet not a friend of Draknek appears to have been involved.Â Woim is the work of dogspawn.net, a one-person studio, and it’s in the same sweet spot of being super-difficult and making you feel like a genius when you solve things.

WoimÂ is a bizarre fusion ofÂ Snake andÂ Sokoban, a 2D block-pushing, worm-growing puzzler. Things begin fairly simply, with rules about negotiating the earth-walled mazes and eating apples to grow your worm long enough to be touching a switch and going through the gate it opens at the same time, without getting stuck in a corridor or trapped by your own pink booty. There are 50 puzzles here, and as much as I’d like to pretend I’ve already finished them, look, it’s really hard, OK? Mechanics change as you progress, and the game is never so rude as to think you need any of it explained. And crucially, you’veÂ got a rewind button, so you can experiment as much as you like until you figure out what you’re supposed to do with mud, or eggs, or jigsaws.

You’ll need that “undo” button, too, and it’s an unlimited, ever-generous option that lets you rewind every move you’ve played in a level at excellent speed, taking away that agonizing feeling of having found yourself trapped in a dead end and being forced to restart. Zipping back as far as you need, perhaps before you ate that one extra apple that made you too long to escape a looping tunnel, ensures things always feel like they’re progressing, not resetting.

And then there’s the first time you get chopped in half.

This is what makesÂ Woim so delightful, the way it springs new elements on you rather than handholds you toward them. It’s a game I felt like I wasÂ experiencing rather than being led through, which feels splendid. It’s a cheerful, lighthearted presentation of some incredibly well-constructed puzzles, and without a glimmer of smugness.

It turns out I started playingÂ Woim on some sort of artificially induced super-high difficulty, because due to some sort of glitch with my Xbox controller, the game was constantly pulling me downward as if I were fighting gravity in its top-down 2D underworld. This, it seems, was not intended, but I’d like to pitch it as a feature for a sequel, because it caused all manner of interesting techniques to be needed. I almost reviewed that game, the one I thought this game was, and while I had some very serious issues with how you’re supposed to pull off some especially tricky moves, it kind of all worked! Someone make that game too; apparently I’ll give it a lot of praise.

In the meantime, the actually intended version ofÂ Woim is fantastic, too! And for $10, you would be a dreadful, slithering creep to object.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

Today's article is about ParkourV, but it is also about the vast graveyard of mods I have hitherto infected Grand Theft Auto 5 with and which then did not work. Did you know I at some point tried to install some sort of dating mod? I'd forgotten, but then there it was, asking me precisely how I would like to rizz up a babe as I initiated a frontflip from the roof of an 80-storey building.

Why? Because to make ParkourV work, I had to update my installation of ScriptHookVDotNet, one of those fundamental building blocks of modding on GTA, a bit like the Skyrim Script Extender for Skyrim. So now we live in a world in which I am constantly hitting keys and accidentally reanimating the corpses of mods I had installed and written off months ago. That's the world we have now and we're just gonna keep living in it.

Anyway. Parkour. The thing is, you see, GTA 5 is not really designed for parkour. Franklin, Trevor and Mike don't have the points of articulation for it. Attempting to do flips, then, just sort of rotates your entire body below the diaphragm while your head and chest area remain bolt upright, rigid in such a way that you could feasibly fly a flag from your own thorax.

Which looks odd. Nevertheless, it is pretty fun to scoot and roll your way through Los Santos. At one point, I attempted a double frontflip in the middle of a part of the map that had been deleted for some reason. It didn't quite work out, and I ended up colliding with and possibly killing a man in a fursuit.

#3771. Mass Effect petition has enough signatures for the Canadian Government to potentially save BioWare

Following news of EA's decision to shut down iconic RPG studio BioWare, Canadian fans of the studio have escalated their grievances to the governmental level, calling on the Canadian Government to step in and save the Canadian studio from closure, seemingly after Canada's New Democratic Party leader Avi Lewis called on the government to do so.

Fans have submitted a petition to the Canadian House of Commons arguing for the government to find a way for BioWare to continue, such as through funding that allows the studio to buy the Mass Effect and other IPs and go independent.

The petition, number e-7898, argues that "BioWare is one of Canada's most important cultural exports" and that the studio's closure by its American parent company "represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy."

"BioWare's productions champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights that are at the centre of Canada's national identity," it continued.

The petition opened for signatures on 4th of November, and has already amassed 1,700 signatures. By law, petitions that surpass 500 valid signatures from Canadian citizens or residents are entered into the House of Commons' agenda, meaning they will be presented in front of the parliament.

As encouraging as that may be, it's worth keeping in mind that it may not result in meaningful change. Even if the Canadian Government agrees with the petition's goals, it cannot force EA to sell BioWare or its various IPs.

EA notably didn't shop the studio around before closing it down, and the publisher has a history of closing down owned studios rather than selling them off. EA has also kept the IPs of its various shuttered studios.

The community's reaction to BioWare's closure has taken different forms. Hundreds of thousands signed a different petition to save Mass Effect. The people behind the movement have purchased billboards in Times Square in New York City to advertise it, with plans for more outside The Game Awards ceremony in December.

Meanwhile, former BioWare developers have spoken about the last days of BioWare, and the work they've poured into Mass Effect Universe, the studio's final project before it was shuttered.

Last month we got news that Wing Commander 3, the FMV space-combat sim with perhaps the highest concentration of Mark Hamill in any videogame, would be getting a remaster. Producer Jim Vessella is heading up the project, and revealed it during a presentation at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo.

What he did not reveal, it turns out, is that five other Wing Commander games—plus Road Rash—would be getting their own dolled-up re-releases, and that they'd all be dropping on Steam, GOG, and the EA App today as part of a larger bundle of 25 "EA Classics". Personally, I'll just be glad to have a copy of Theme Hospital where all my other games are. On the remaster front, EA pinky promises it hasn't mucked the games up. "Each Anniversary Edition preserves the original look, feel and creative intent of the game, with quality-of-life updates to support modern systems, controls, improve performance and make the titles more approachable without compromising their authenticity."

You know what? I'm inclined to believe it. Vessella, who's more or less become the face of EA's old-game preservation and restoration efforts, also had a big hand in the work on the Command and Conquer Remastered Collection, and that was rather excellent even without access to the source footage of those games' FMV cutscenes, which seems to not be an issue here.

EA says the remasters are the fruit of "the discovery of a physical media vault containing thousands of Betacam, VHS, and D1 tapes alongside other media assets", while "the digitization process recovered the supposedly lost Master FMV sequences for these seven legendary titles, which were meticulously re-edited to restore the over 1,500 cinematic scenes across these games".

#3768. Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes

Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today, has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles.

As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters, citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa.

Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs.

The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages.

PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices, on several occasions. Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles, with the most recent having taken place in August.

That same crisis pushed one of Nintendo's longtime ROM suppliers to exit the business, opting instead to focus on the more lucrative business segments. ROM memory is used in Switch cartridges, though Nintendo hasn't commented on the news.

Incidentally, Switch 2 hardware sales have been in decline for several quarters now compared to its banner launch in 2025. Still, Switch 2 sales are tracking ahead of the Switch 1.

#3766. How to Stock a Flu Season Cabinet That Eases Symptoms Without Stress

A ready medicine cabinet takes the panic out of flu season. Spending a few minutes to audit yours now means you can focus on rest instead of a midnight drugstore run when a fever hits. Here’s what belongs on the shelf, why each item earns its spot and how to use it well.

Pharmacies and major medical centers are urging families to audit their medicine cabinets before symptoms force a late-night trip to the drugstore. The checklists are specific, and they overlap across institutions.

A working thermometer tops nearly every list. University of Rochester Medicine defines a fever in adults as a temperature of 100.4°F or higher, the same threshold used for children. Average body temperature sits at 98.6°F but can vary from 97.5°F to 99.5°F throughout the day.

Other essentials include saline nasal spray, pain relievers like acetaminophen and ibuprofen, decongestants, cough expectorants, cough suppressants, cough drops, honey, herbal tea, electrolyte drinks and a humidifier.

The first reason is symptom relief. The flu brings fevers, headaches, coughs, body aches, sore throats and congestion, and no single product covers all of it. That’s why clinicians recommend keeping a mix of pain relievers, decongestants, expectorants and suppressants on hand.

Infectious disease specialist Steven Gordon, MD, told Cleveland Clinic, “There are a lot of great over-the-counter medications that you can use for symptom relief. You can also get a flu and cold medication to help cut down on the nasal stuffiness and the cough that you might have.”

Hydration matters just as much. Fever and fluid loss can quickly deplete electrolytes, slowing recovery. Registered dietitian Beth Czerwony told Cleveland Clinic, “Your body needs hydration more than any specific food when you’re fighting the flu, especially early on.”

Herbal teas, soup and electrolyte drinks all work toward that same end, easing congestion while replacing what fever burns off.

Fever hits the household. If a thermometer reads 100.4°F or higher, that’s the flu-fever threshold for both adults and children, per University of Rochester Medicine. Mayo Clinic recommends different thermometer types by age. Contactless forehead or rectal work best for infants under 3 months, oral or ear suits ages 4 and older, and ear or oral is preferred for seniors 65 and up. Forehead models of any kind should be avoided for seniors. Match the device to the person before you need it.

Confusion in the pharmacy aisle. OTC products interact with other medications more often than most buyers realize. CVS Pharmacy’s Nicole Henry, PharmD, recommends asking for help before buying. “Your pharmacist can help answer questions and identify considerations based on your symptoms, age, other medications and individual health needs.”

Read every label and talk with the pharmacist on duty before adding anything to the cart.

Dry indoor air sets in. If a healthcare provider recommends a humidifier, The Thread by Walgreens advises cool mist models for homes with children, distilled or filtered water instead of tap, placement about 3 feet from the bed, indoor humidity held between 30 percent and 50 percent and cleaning every two to three days. People with COPD or dust mite allergies should check with a provider first, since humidified air can worsen their symptoms.

One realistic next step today, check the thermometer and make sure it works. A reading at or above 100.4°F is the signal that the rest of the cabinet starts earning its place.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on a recent podcast that "from a global allocation perspective, actually it's quite terrible to have everyone have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and be used 5% of the time."

Altman was talking about people running AI models locally rather than relying on data centers, which allow RAM usage to be maxed out in this "very supply-constrained environment." What many heard and responded to—PC gamers in particular—was resentment directed at those of us who don't run AI companies, but would still like to have and use our own personal computers, as a treat.

In an exchange on X this week, Altman said that his remark was "taken out of context" and that he actually wants "the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers."

"I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time," Altman said.

Altman's argument for increased memory production is no consolation to the tech enthusiasts and gamers who've been priced out of new hardware by his company and the rest of the AI industry. What we've been calling the RAMpocalypse hasn't just affected high-end PCs, either: In the lead-up to GTA 6's console launch, a PlayStation Pro is $900, if you can even find one.

The bitter reaction to Altman's comment also comes from concerns that big tech companies want to push gamers off of local hardware so that they can rent us cloud computing. For an audience that's already disgruntled about the erosion of game ownership, the thought of losing control over our own hardware is not palatable, however much cloud streaming services like Nvidia's GeForce Now have improved.

That concern is now coupled with the generative AI-heavy future that tech leaders are pushing. If generative AI is best delivered as a cloud service, and the games industry is going to increasingly incorporate generative AI into games, it follows that we will be pushed toward cloud computing.

Nvidia DLSS pioneer Bryan Catanzaro made a comment to that effect at a GDC panel I attended earlier this year. Speaking about hypothetical games built with AI "world models," Catanzaro noted that we probably won't run those models locally, because "AI is fundamentally much more efficient in the cloud."
